title: Typed Cache Tensors Design Review, Round 3
eyebrow: Round-3 review of the second codex revision of the design for issue #4525 (positron-ai/tron)
h1: Did the second revision close the round-2 findings, and is the typed KV-cache tensor design implementable now?
meta: Reviewed 2026-09-22 UTC by Claude (Fable 5.1) for jhan. Design reviewed: [status/design-new-tensor-type.html](design-new-tensor-type.html), second revision by codex after the [round-2 review](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r2.html) (finalized 2026-09-22 06:24 UTC, 121,774 bytes, sha256 5dea1702). Sources pinned to main f46e48ba (the design's snapshot), main 2880c3aa9b (the tip the design's S15-S20 cite), the live main tip 1400fa4481 (fetched 2026-09-22 ~07:00 UTC; none of the design's files changed since 2880c3aa9b) and PR 4424 head 30c4ac82cb.
short_version: The second revision resolved 60 of the 87 open items (64 round-2 findings plus 23 round-1 residuals). 25 are partly resolved, 2 are deferred to jhan, none is unresolved and none regressed.

This round found 52 new defects: 1 major, 27 minor, 24 notes. The major one is a single missing sentence: the design no longer says how detail::scaled_v_expr, the weighted V sum in kv_cache.hpp, obtains the packed address under the new access rule (G01). The other items an implementer would stop on are the t_amx_numerics fixture route (G22), the constraint mechanism (G09) and the D5 wording (G04).

Verdict: accept with changes. All three judges say so; two of three say the design is not yet implementable until G01 and G22 are written. After those two edits and the eleven regressions and residuals listed in section 7, another agent can implement the parent from this page.

words: tron
the inference program under test; its source is the positron-ai/tron repository
PR 4424, the child

the open draft pull request "VNNI K: store the K cache of 128-dimension heads in the AMX VNNI layout, with a shared block save" (branch jhan-amx-vnniK, head 30c4ac82cb). After the new parent PR exists, PR 4424 is rebased onto it and is then called the child
the parent PR
the new pull request that issue #4525 asks for: typed access to the existing V and K caches on main, with no new layout
Ben, the reviewer
the tron maintainer who reviewed PR 4424 on 2026-09-21 (a worker-index question, a review asking for typed tensors, and an API sketch). The revised design calls him "the reviewer"
issue #4525
the GitHub issue codex created for the parent PR; jhan edited its title and first sentence on 2026-09-22 00:10 UTC; unchanged since
KV cache, K, V
the saved key (K) and value (V) vectors of earlier tokens; attention reads them
page, slot, head, D

a page holds 64 token positions; a slot is the cache region of one layer (or of several layers that share it); a head is one attention head; D is the head size, the number of values per token per head (128 for PR 4424's models)
bf16
the 16-bit brain floating-point format used for cached K and V
AMX, AVX-512, 16-lane and 8-lane builds

AMX and AVX-512 are CPU instruction sets. tron's vector width TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 16 fp32 values with AVX-512 (the 16-lane build) and 8 without (the 8-lane build); the 8-lane build stores V row-major, so it has no pair-interleaved V
packed V (pair-interleaved V)
today's V storage in the 16-lane build: for each dimension, tokens 2p and 2p+1 sit next to each other. Element offset = (token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2
native K
today's K storage: one token's D values consecutive in memory (row-major)
blocked packed K (VNNI K)
PR 4424's K storage for 128-dimension heads: two consecutive dimensions of one token share a 4-byte unit, and 16 tokens share one 64-byte line
expr, view, const_view, tensor

tron's expression interface (h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp), its typed pointer views over regularly laid-out memory and their read-only form (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp), and its owning arrays (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp)
kv_block
the struct that holds K then V for one head of one slot in one page (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp)
set_v, get_v, append_v, scaled_v, v_data
today's V functions in kv_cache.hpp: write one token, read one token, copy one token between pages, compute the weighted V sum, and return the raw pointer of a V plane
save_v_impl
the model function (h/tron/models/model.hpp) that stores one token's V into the cache during a forward pass; it calls page::set_v
Zero-Initialized V Slots invariant

the rule in kv_cache.hpp that every even-token V write zeroes its odd partner row. The weighted sum reads a whole pair even when the token count is odd, and NaN times 0 is NaN, so the padding row must be zero
arena, book
an arena is one allocated memory region holding cache blocks; book is the class that owns the arenas and the pages
EAGLE
the speculative model; its cache adds one extra physical KV slot and a separate embedding buffer (x_data); it requires uniform geometry
GOF, page_info
group of four: four tokens of K and V staged for the FPGA's hardware KV cache; the staging code reaches a page's rows through the page_info callbacks in h/tron/gof.hpp (namespace tron::hardware)
CI, Nix test build, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, TRON_K_VNNI

CI is the automated build and test. The Nix test build is the required CI lane. The two CMake options compile the AMX attention kernels and PR 4424's K layout; the Nix lane sets neither. Issue #3997 tracks the AMX gap
codex, the design, the second revision

codex is the agent jhan asked to answer Ben; the design is the page it wrote, status/design-new-tensor-type.html; the second revision is the version finalized 2026-09-22 06:24 UTC (121,774 bytes) after the round-2 review. It is the version reviewed here

the first Claude review of the original design (2026-09-22 ~03:00 UTC), archived as [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html). Its 58 retained findings are F01-F59 (finders) and C01-C09 (completeness critic)

It graded the 58 round-1 findings (35 resolved, 20 partly, 3 deferred) and added 64 findings N01-N62 (finders) and M01-M08 (critic). The design cites these ids in brackets, for example [N13]
round 3, G.. and H.. ids, the 87 open items

this review. G.. are new findings from the ten finders, H.. from the completeness critic. The 87 open items are the 64 round-2 findings plus the 23 round-1 findings that round 2 graded partly or deferred; section 3 grades each against the second revision
v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view, v_vnni_row, detail::v_vnni_access

the design's names for the packed-V owner (the aligned array inside the cache block), the typed rank-2 view over it, its logical row expression, and the friend helper that alone may read the packed pointer
append_v_row, load_row, copy_token

the design's typed bulk operations: write one token's V row into the packed plane (an even token zeroes its odd partner), read one row out, copy one token between planes. The design adds no copy_plane for V
kv_cache_fwd.hpp, v_vnni.hpp, k_vnni.hpp
the design's new headers: a declarations-only header (no intrinsics) that amx_attn_iface.hpp includes, the V definitions header, and the child's K definitions header under h/tron/tensor/
native_k_view, const_native_k_view
the design's aliases for today's row-major K view and its read-only form (view / const_view with explicit strides Cols, 1); no new K storage class in the parent
k_storage, k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, k_packed

the child's typed K storage as the design specifies it: a std::conditional_t that selects the packed owner for 128-dimension heads and the existing array otherwise, its view, and the accessor that replaces the raw k_vnni_plane pointer
decision record, Q1-Q4, D5
the table in design section 2: four questions for Ben with a proposed choice, a fallback if rejected, and a record status, plus D5, the native-K typing scope that jhan requested
TRON_IGNORE_NAN
a compile definition that tron sets in every non-Debug GCC/Clang build (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:293); with it, the generic bf16 conversion does not preserve NaNs whose upper mantissa bits are zero
page_supports_uniform_kv_access
a compile-time probe in t/t_llama_unit.cpp:105 that checks a page type offers the uniform K/V accessors; the design has it rewritten for the typed get_v destination
8-lane baseline limit

the design's statement that t_llama_unit and t_heterogeneous_scheduler do not compile in the 8-lane build at unmodified main (they call the 16-lane-only set_v/get_v), so the parent's 8-lane acceptance excludes them
RUN_TESTS, passage marker

in the required GCP Nix workflow, RUN_TESTS is true only when the test identity has not passed before or the run is a rerun; the passage marker records a passed identity so a later run may skip the tests
for_each_active_slot, storage_location, slot_base
book members the design reuses to enumerate physical KV slots with their compile-time geometry, to learn which arena a slot lives in, and to compute its address
checker, re-grader, finder, verifier, critic, judge

review agents of this round. A checker graded a batch of known items against the second revision; two re-graders (a source-truth lens and a fairness lens) independently re-graded each; the majority of the three decided. Ten finders looked for new defects; one merge agent removed duplicates; three verifiers tried to refute each candidate; a finding survived when at least two could not. A completeness critic added candidates that went through the same verification. Three judges gave independent implementability verdicts
resolved, partly, deferred, unresolved, regressed
disposition statuses; the table in section 3 gives the meaning of each
blocker, major, minor, note
severities; the table in section 4 gives the meaning of each
detail::scaled_v_expr, the weighted V sum

the struct in kv_cache.hpp that computes the attention-weighted sum of a page's V rows on the AVX-512 path; today it reads the packed plane through a raw pointer. G01 is about how it gets that address under the new types
t_amx_numerics PV case
the unit test case that compares the AMX PV kernel (weights times V) with the AVX path; today it hand-packs a std::vector page and passes its pointer to the kernel
lint-notes
a separate Make target that checks every 'See Note [X]' comment has a matching Note definition; the required Lint CI check runs it, make lint does not

dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation asked for three things. (1) Class definitions complete in both builds: design-r3.txt:281 and :372 say so. (2) Operation bodies and packed-V test cases only under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16, with no 8-lane pair extraction: design-r3.txt:282 guards "packed operation bodies and packed-only tests", :281 says no 8-lane SIMD implementations are required, and the two t_llama_unit rows that build a packed owner now say "16-lane build" (:436, :441). (3) Typed kernel declarations and fakes unconditional: :281 keeps the declarations at both widths and :453 names "unconditional fake definitions". The round-2 sentence "Derive a pair chunk's width from chunk_size" is removed (design-wdiff.txt:899-901).

Facts checked. The fake kernel definitions sit outside any #ifdef at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:166-190; the only guarded region is the test-case block :192-214. That test is registered without a condition at t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:596 (the last enclosing if() block ends at :381). The typed signature at design-r3.txt:277 takes v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> by value, so class completeness is the requirement the design names. The kernel declarations at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b:219-233 are under no preprocessor condition (grep of the file finds only the namespace lines :114 and :240). Every AMX call site in self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b is under #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (:259, :281, :1429, :1531, :1571, :1748) and that macro is a #error when TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16 (:30-36), so no 8-lane code calls a packed operation. The 8-lane save path is pg.v<>().set() (model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2833-2837) and 8-lane V stays a row-major array (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2199-2201). The source-lens verifier's warning not to make the whole 8-lane row compile-only is also respected: design-r3.txt:454 compares baseline/head builds of tron, and :270 leaves the 8-lane path unchanged so nothing new needs 8-lane execution.

dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation (intent lens) has five parts. Four are present. (1) The two suites are named as not compiling at 8 lanes, with the reason that set_v/get_v are 16-lane only (design-r3.txt:457); the S16 links point at the exact sites the recommendation named (t_llama_unit.cpp L84-L123 holds the page_supports_uniform_kv_access probe with get_v at :107; L1199-L1204 holds the check_wide_scaled_v instantiations whose set_v call is at :142; heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp L441-L444 holds the set_v call at :443). (2) The 8-lane check is builds of tron and t_amx_dispatch_dtype (:454). (4) The two suites are excluded from the acceptance target and their diagnostics recorded (:457). (5) The t_llama_unit behavior rows say "16-lane build" (:436, :441). Part (3) is missing: the corrected recommendation asked the row to say that running t_amx_dispatch_dtype is not evidence because it executes only a placeholder. The row instead says "Run applicable dispatch cases if the baseline builds". No dispatch case is applicable in this row: at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b the four real sections are under #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (:192-209) and the #else branch compiles only TEST_CASE("AMX dispatch dtype test skipped (dispatch not compiled)") with SUCCEED("build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH - nothing to test") (:210-214). The general rule at :445 forbids counting placeholders, so the slip is minor, but the row's own cue points the other way.

Facts checked. kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1616 `#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16` opens the set_v/get_v declarations (:1622-1673), :1674 `#else` gives only v() and v_ptr(), :1725 `#endif`; definitions are under :2281-2532. t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b calls get_v at :107, :2038, :2539, :2761, :2824 and set_v at :142, :1723, :2533, :2535, :2568, :2569, :2690, :2705, :2721, :2792, :2802; the file's only chunk guards are :793-800, :817-823, :1551-1555, :1573-1578, :1732-1767, :1922-1926, so the verifiers' "file-wide 16-lane assumption" holds and the design's decision not to repair it in the parent is right. t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp@2880c3aa9b:443 calls page->set_v and the file has no TRON_CHUNK_SIZE, AVX512 or #if line (grep). t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:586-592 registers t_llama_unit and :572-575 registers t_heterogeneous_scheduler outside any if() block. The design's "inferred from source" and "Insufficient data" labels match the verifiers' own status: nobody compiled the 8-lane build. Small imprecision, not a defect: the heterogeneous test calls set_v only; the joint phrase "set_v/get_v" at :457 is exact for t_llama_unit.

dispositions.new_defect: Claim: the new Debug configuration row tells the agent to "Run targeted conversion cases using make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target" (design-r3.txt:455). That command changes the build type only when Make re-runs the CMake configure step, and Make re-runs it only when the gen/config/test stamp is stale. Source: GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:880-881 `gen/t_%: gen/config/test $(HEADERS) $(SOURCES)` runs only `cmake --build gen --target $(notdir $@)`; the configure recipe `cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) ...` is the rule body of gen/config/test (:538-543) and runs only when a prerequisite is newer than the stamp; gen/.preset_stamp (:299-303) records CMAKE_PRESET only, not BUILD_TYPE. So in a gen/ that was already configured as RelWithDebInfo, `make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit` keeps the cached RelWithDebInfo and TRON_IGNORE_NAN stays defined; the agent would then test the macro-defined policy while believing it tested the Debug policy. Mitigation already in the design: "Use a separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair" (design-r3.txt:449) and "Confirm the macro is absent" (:455), so the risk is low. Also the sentence "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo" (:455) describes the same stamp mechanism incompletely: a later plain `make` restores RelWithDebInfo only when the stamp is stale. Recommendation: change the row to "Run make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit only in a freshly configured gen/ (delete gen/config/test first); the Make configure recipe re-runs only when that stamp is stale, and gen/.preset_stamp records the preset, not the build type. Confirm the macro is absent in compile_commands.json before running."

design-r3.txt:331 "Generic fp32s_to_bf16s also truncates, but preserves a NaN with only discarded mantissa bits when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent. That correction sets the lowest retained mantissa bit, not necessarily the quiet-NaN bit. All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro, including the native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds. Preserve the behavior selected by the actual macro."
design-r3.txt:334 "| fp32 0x7F800001 : NaN with upper seven mantissa bits zero | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity | bf16 0x7F81 : NaN | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity |"
design-r3.txt:336 "Expected bit patterns from the source conversion rules, not measured test results. Only the generic conversion changes with the macro. Branch test expectations on #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN."
design-r3.txt:437 "Select generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN , using section 6's bit table. Check Debug and non-Debug builds for the two policies."
design-r3.txt:549 (section 9) "| F41 | Correct the fp32 NaN example and select generic expectations by the actual build macro. [Design section] | No new NaN behavior is requested. Test both policies. |"
dispositions.assessment:
The round-2 residual had three parts plus two re-grader additions. Three parts are now in the body and are factually right; the two additions are missing.

Present and verified:
1. Worked example: the table row (design-r3.txt:334) gives 0x7F800001 -> 0x7F80 (packed) / 0x7F81 (generic, macro absent) / 0x7F80 (generic, macro defined). Checked against h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:93-108 (OR 0x00010000 where exponent field == 0x7f800000 and low 16 bits != 0, then shift right 16) and kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2382 (`_mm512_srli_epi32(..., 16)` in the float set_v). "upper seven mantissa bits zero" correctly replaces the loose "no upper mantissa bits" (fp32 mantissa bits 22-16). RIGHT.
2. Build-type sentence: "All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro, including the native and required Nix RelWithDebInfo builds" (design-r3.txt:331) matches src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-294, CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37 and nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:80. The plain direction ("outside Debug both paths truncate identically") is carried by the table's last column and by "Only the generic conversion changes with the macro" (:336). RIGHT.
3. Test-row guidance: design-r3.txt:437 tells the author to branch generic NaN expectations on #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN and to run both build types; the Debug configuration exists at :455. This is the first branch of the residual's either/or. RIGHT.
4. Section 9 row 549 now matches the body (the example exists), which closes the fairness re-grader's point.

Missing (the re-grader additions):
(a) The design never says the macro is a PUBLIC compile option of the tron target, so a reader may think only library code is affected. Source: src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292 `target_compile_options(tron PUBLIC ...)`; t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:190 links each test PRIVATE to its LIBRARIES, and t_llama_unit lists `tron` (:586-587). The design's #ifdef guidance works only because of this propagation.
(b) The existing precedent t/t_bf16.cpp@2880c3aa9b:97-110 ("bf16 preserves nan", comment "this test may fail on some hardware if IGNORE_NAN is set", NaNs built from inf - inf) is not named, and the advice "use quiet NaNs for expectations shared by both paths; put the signalling case 0x7F800001 only on the packed append path" is absent. Because the design chose the #ifdef branch, (b) is helpful rather than required.

Both omissions are low risk: an implementer following :437 and :455 builds the right tests.
dispositions.residual: Add after the sentence at design-r3.txt:331 "All non-Debug GCC/Clang builds define the macro ...": "TRON_IGNORE_NAN is a PUBLIC compile option of the tron target [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-295 @2880c3aa9b], so test executables that link tron, including t_llama_unit [t/CMakeLists.txt:586-587], compile with it too; an #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN in test code therefore sees the same value as the library." Optionally add to the Bits row (design-r3.txt:437): "Precedent: t/t_bf16.cpp:97-110 (\"bf16 preserves nan\") avoids the build dependence by using quiet NaNs (inf - inf). Use quiet NaNs for expectations shared by both paths; put the signalling case 0x7F800001 only on the packed append path, which always truncates."

votes.reason: Round 1 asked for the exact NaN divergence rule, the fp32 worked example, and a warning that expected bits differ per path and per build type; the round-1 verifiers withdrew the fp16 example. This matches bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:92-109 (OR 0x00010000, which becomes bf16 bit 0 after the 16-bit shift) and src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295. The design's #ifdef branch is a valid alternative to that precedent.

votes.reason: The round-2 residual asked for three things. (1) A worked example replacing "an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits". The bit table now reads "fp32 0x7F800001 : NaN with upper seven mantissa bits zero | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity | bf16 0x7F81 : NaN | bf16 0x7F80 : +infinity" [design-r3.txt:333-334]. I checked the bits: 0x7F800001 has exponent 0xFF and mantissa 0x000001, so mantissa bits 22 to 16 are zero and the value is a signalling NaN. Truncation to the upper 16 bits gives 0x7F80 (+infinity). fp32s_to_bf16s without the macro ORs 0x00010000 [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp@2880c3aa9b:106] and shifts right by 16 [108], giving 0x7F81. With the macro it gives 0x7F80. The sentence "That correction sets the lowest retained mantissa bit, not necessarily the quiet-NaN bit" [design-r3.txt:331] is right (bit 16 of fp32 versus bit 22). (2) A sentence that the macro is defined for every non-Debug build including the RelWithDebInfo Nix test build. Present at design-r3.txt:331, verified against src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295 and nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:80. (3) A test-row warning that generic NaN bits depend on the build type, with a guard or a restriction. The Bits row chooses the guard: "Select generic NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN ... Check Debug and non-Debug builds" [design-r3.txt:437], and a Debug configuration row exists [design-r3.txt:455]. The fairness re-grader's point is also addressed: the section 9 row "Correct the fp32 NaN example" [design-r3.txt:549] now describes a body that contains the example, and the direction is plain because the "macro defined" column equals the packed column. The withdrawn fp16 example stays out: "The fp16 input path keeps its existing hardware conversion behavior" [design-r3.txt:336]. Two optional additions from the round-2 re-graders were not taken: the word PUBLIC (the option's scope) is not stated, and the precedent test "bf16 preserves nan" that uses quiet NaNs only [t/t_bf16.cpp@2880c3aa9b:97-100] is not named. Both were offered as alternatives, not requirements, so they are not residuals.

Locate the enclosing Catch test functions through source lines for even/odd V append, packed token copy, and weighted sums. Locate surviving allocation/restore instantiations. Forced-inline helpers may have no separate symbol."

dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation (all three verifier lenses) asked for: (1) a method to locate the inlined bodies by source line or by the enclosing non-inlined callers, without telling the agent to look for set_v< or append_v< as symbols; (2) a statement that the baseline t_llama_unit has no fp16 set_v body, with the harness-or-record alternative; and it dropped the optimization-level demand. All three are in the body.

Facts checked:
- "RelWithDebInfo build type": CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37 for preset native. RIGHT.
- "The build adds -O3; do not assume the preset's nominal -O2 is the effective final setting": src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-294 adds -O3 PUBLIC on tron for every non-Debug GCC/Clang build; t_llama_unit links tron (t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:190, :586-587), and per-target options follow CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO on the compile line, so -O3 is the effective level. RIGHT, and more accurate than the verifiers' "(-O2 -g)".
- "gen/t_llama_unit": CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:66 `set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})`; preset native binaryDir is ${sourceDir}/gen (CMakePresets.json:34). RIGHT. (Note only: the S17 link "[Binary output directory]" points at CMakeLists.txt#L67, one line after the set() at :66; that link belongs to N60/S17, not N40.)
- `objdump -d -l --no-show-raw-insn -C`: -l is --line-numbers and needs the -g that RelWithDebInfo carries. Consistent with the design-text lens correction.
- "Forced-inline helpers may have no separate symbol": set_v (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1621-1673) and append_v (:1872) are TRON(inline); h/common/attributes.hpp@2880c3aa9b:77-78 defines tron_inline as `inline __attribute__((always_inline))`. RIGHT. allocate_kv_group (:1199) and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage (:962-963) carry no forced-inline attribute, so "surviving allocation/restore instantiations" is the right hedge.
- "The baseline suite does not instantiate fp16 append": `git grep fp16 2880c3aa9b -- t/t_llama_unit.cpp` hits only :1081 (a scale constant); every set_v call in that file (:142, :796, :1554, :1723, :1923, :2533-2802) passes bf16 or float buffers; no fp16 set_v caller exists in h/, src/ or t/ at 2880c3aa9b. RIGHT.
- The harness-or-record alternative (:487) matches the correction's either/or, and the text names no set_v< / append_v< symbols to search for.
- Section 9 row 527 matches the body.

dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation asked the design to state the parameter type per accessor and give the reason. Both are done. set_k_row and get_k_row take tron's contiguous row view family (const_view for the source, view for the destination), the same family the parent uses for set_v/get_v at design-r3.txt:255. set_k_block keeps 16 raw const bf16* entries. Each choice carries a reason: the view flags preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties and no copy is needed [design-r3.txt:405]; the pointer array is kept because absent lanes are null and the destination plane, not the source rows, carries the layout type [design-r3.txt:406].

Facts checked:
- Template parameter order is view<T, aligned, dma, Dim, Stride> [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:22-28]. The rank-1 specialization is view<T, aligned, dma, seq<d0>, sseq<s0>> [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:115-116]. The design's spelled types const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> follow that order.
- The child's parameters are `const bf16* row` and `bf16* row` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1701-1702, :1737-1738]. Conversion to bf16 happens before the call: `view<bf16, true, false, seq<geometry.kv.head_size>>{conv[i]}.set(kout)` [h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2922-2924, :2936-2938]. So fixing the element type to bf16 matches the child.
- kout is already a view with a .data member [model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2918-2920]. The GOF callback passes caller-owned scratch `dest` to get_k_row [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655]. "Wrap scratch without copying" applies to these sites.
- scatter_row loads the source row with _mm512_loadu_si512 (an unaligned load) [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:142] and gather_row stores with _mm512_storeu_si512 (an unaligned store) [:226]. store_block loads with loadu [:201]. So "These K routines do not acquire V's stronger alignment requirement" is right, and "Preserve the existing gather/scatter instructions" names real instructions (_mm512_i32scatter_epi32 at :143, _mm512_i32gather_epi32 at :224).
- set_k_block takes `const bf16* const rows[k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16]` [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1723-1728]. The caller zero-initializes `const bf16* rows[K_STORE_BLOCK_16] = {};` so absent lanes are null [model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2929]. "null entries for absent lanes" is right.
- Ben's sketch uses std::span<const bf16, Dims> for the K row (github-review.json, comment 5765866077). The design states its deliberate alternative and why, which the recommendation allowed.

One observation that is not part of N32 and not a new error: the child's set_k_row/get_k_row also serve the native (row-major) layout through memcpy via k_at(i_page).data [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1707-1709, :1745-1747]. The design row says "Call typed store_row / load_row" without saying what the native branch does with the view parameter. The round-2 text had the same sentence, so this is pre-existing and outside the corrected recommendation. An implementer can keep the memcpy from the view's data or use the native row view's set().

dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation asked for one paragraph that (1) lists what becomes local to the K type, (2) lists what stays outside it with the files, and (3) opens by answering the request's expectation that the VNNI-K change becomes "a local change within the new tensor data type, not at main function" [codex-add-tensor-type.md:16-18].

What the design now has: a heading that names the topic [design-r3.txt:418] and one bullet that lists the outside categories [design-r3.txt:425]. The categories map to real child code: storage selection = the layout_on conditional in kv_cache.hpp; score arithmetic = qk_group in h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:248 and qk_vnni_128x4 in h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@30c4ac82cb:251, called from self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1436-1438 and :1636; worker coordination = k_store_shared and save_k in model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2806, :2953-3079; generated calls = ingest/src/TronCpp.hs; scratch callbacks = k_head_fn's scratch parameter [h/tron/gof.hpp@30c4ac82cb:78] and its caller [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655]; build option = TRON_K_VNNI in CMakeLists.txt; workflow setting = .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml; tests. All of these files are in the child's 25-file diff (git diff --name-only c7844ca2ce 30c4ac82cb). So the outside list is right as far as it goes.

What is missing: (a) the bullet names categories, not files, so the reader must collect file names from design-r3.txt:390-392 and :407-408; (b) the "inside the K type" half is not in the same place (it is spread over :391, :392 and :405-407); (c) no sentence states that the request's expectation holds only in part. The corrected recommendation asked for one sentence with two parts: how the test fills poison (64 typed store_row calls or memcpy into the owner), and where k_vnni::index lives (constexpr free function, or its new home). Both parts are now in the body.

Poison fill. Line 416 says "Fill poison with 64 typed row saves". That is the first option the recommendation offered. It is valid: each token owns disjoint slots [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:28-29 "Token i owns column (i % 16) of token block (i / 16) in every panel"], and 64 tokens x 128 dimensions = 8,192 elements = the whole plane [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:81-82 static_assert N_PANELS_16 * PANEL_ELEMS_512 == PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128]. The poison bits survive a typed row save: scatter_row moves 32-bit lanes with _mm512_loadu_si512 and _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 and does no float conversion [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:139-146], and line 405 keeps those instructions. So both POISON_0XA5A5 and the NaN poison 0x7FC1 [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:51, 257] are stored bit-exactly. The current direct plane writes at t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:107-109, 190-192, 286-288 are what this replaces.

Index location. Line 391 says k_vnni::index is "the existing constexpr free function", moves it to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, and keeps its spelling. Source: `constexpr size_t index(size_t token, size_t dim) noexcept` in namespace tron::k_vnni [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:42, 101-107, 310]. The anchor cases (STATIC_REQUIRE = Catch2's compile-time assertion) call it by that spelling [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:80 `using tron::k_vnni::index;`, 81-90], as do the byte-position checks [:120, :143]. So they compile unchanged.

Size fact. Line 401 states a 16,384-byte owner for 64 tokens by 128 dimensions. Source: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:22 "64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB". This is the size the memcmp against a same-size reference buffer [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:202, 229] needs, so the verifier's premise correction is also satisfied.

Every checkable fact in the fix is right.

The round-2 residual asked for one decision: what the index anchors call after the K mapping moves, with one spelling picked (public constexpr k_vnni::index in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, or a static member of k_vnni_view). The re-graders added two precisions: the byte-position checks call the same function, and prefill/poison writes and plane-to-plane copies need a stated form.

The decision is made. Line 391 keeps k_vnni::index as "the existing constexpr free function", moves it into h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, and keeps its spelling. Source: `constexpr size_t index(size_t token, size_t dim) noexcept` in namespace tron::k_vnni [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:42, 101-107, 310]. The STATIC_REQUIRE anchors (Catch2's compile-time assertion) call it by that name [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:80 `using tron::k_vnni::index;`, 81-90]. The byte-position checks call the same name [:120 `tron::k_vnni::index(tok, d)`, :143]. "Keep the function spelling" therefore covers both callers, even though line 391 names only "the independent index checks".

Poison and prefill writes. Line 416 chooses 64 typed row saves. This is the first option round-2 N57 offered, and it is bit-exact because scatter_row moves 32-bit lanes without float conversion [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:139-146] and line 405 keeps those instructions. It replaces the direct plane writes at t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:107-109, 190-192, 286-288.

Plane-to-plane copies. The test copies one plane into another with memcpy [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:193, 216]. Line 401 makes the K owner trivially copyable with the V owner's rules, and line 239 keeps same-type copy defaulted for V, so an owner-to-owner assignment is available. The design does not spell this as a sentence, but it follows directly from the stated traits, and this precision was an addition by the re-grader rather than part of the round-1 ask.

The four raw-pointer call kinds in the child test (scatter_row :113, 139, 199, 214, 226, 291; gather_row :129, 232; store_block :201, 228; qk_group :306-309) map onto the typed operations named at design-r3.txt:405-407. Line 416 keeps the ban on the internal friend helper. Line 416 does not force stack allocation, so the heap fixtures at :99, 173-174, 262 may stay.

Every checkable fact in the fix is right.

dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation asked for two things. First, a Short-version clause saying native K keeps its existing view. Second, a step-4 sentence naming the call-site change from the row pointer to the whole-page view. Both are now in the body.

The Short version was rewritten in this revision (design-wdiff.txt:8-20). Sentence 2 now reads "Native K keeps its existing storage and view." [design-r3.txt:9]. That is the qualifier round-1 F30 asked for.

The call-site change is stated in the accessor table [design-r3.txt:266] and in step 4 [design-r3.txt:375]. I checked each fact in it against main at 2880c3aa9b:
- The current caller uses the three-argument row overload and passes k0.data: `const auto k0 = pg.template k<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, 0); amx_attn_h128g4::qk_rowmajor_128x4(k0.data, q_packed, &s_pages[0][0], page::page_size);` [self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1653-1655]. RIGHT.
- `pg` there is `const page& pg` [self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1626], so the two-argument accessor returns the const view.
- The two-argument templated overloads `k(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head)` (non-const and const) return `kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).k_view()` [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1557-1571]. `k_view() const` returns `const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<page_size, head_size>>` [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2215-2219]. So "the whole plane" is RIGHT.
- The default fifth view parameter is `row_major<Dim>` [views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:26,35], and row_major of a two-dimensional seq is sseq<Cols, 1> [seq.hpp@2880c3aa9b:394, 509-510]. So the design's `const_native_k_view` alias with explicit strides [design-r3.txt:222] names the same type the const accessor returns. The call type-matches.
- The current kernel parameter is `const bf16* k_page` [amx_attn_iface.hpp@2880c3aa9b:219]. "from a pointer to the existing read-only matrix view" [design-r3.txt:64] is RIGHT.
- Short-version sentence 3 ("a separate packed-K owner") matches the child storage selection `k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size>` [design-r3.txt:396-400].

Bookkeeping only: the design-text lens suggested adding "Short version and step 4 updated" to the F30 row in section 9. The F30 row [design-r3.txt:538] does not say that. The N45 row [design-r3.txt:516] carries "explain native-K aliases". No body text is missing, so this does not lower the status.

dispositions.assessment:
Both factual errors named by N13 are gone. The round-2 sentence "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" was replaced (design-wdiff.txt lines 597-603 show the OLD/NEW text). The word "lossy" was removed from the section-8 row (design-wdiff.txt lines 1613-1615).

Facts checked in the new text:
- "A missing override uses the expression base's fp32 conversion fallback": RIGHT. h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:111-117@2880c3aa9b reads `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk) { return self().bf16_chunk(i); } else { return fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i)); }`. When B declares no bf16_chunk, both pointers name the base member and compare equal.
- "A wrong signature can fail compilation": RIGHT and hedged as the verifier asked (a mismatched signature makes the `!=` ill-formed at expr.hpp:112; the round-2 source-lens verifier noted g++ 11.4 and clang 19 differ on the noexcept-only case).
- "omitting noexcept does not silently select that fallback": RIGHT per the intent-lens correction (either the override is used or the comparison is a compile error; never silent).
- "Do not claim the fallback corrupts stored bf16 bits" and section 8 "bit-exact fallback": RIGHT. h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109@f46e48bab498 (identical at 2880c3aa9b and 1400fa4481) ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field == 0x7f800000 AND the low 16 bits != 0, then shifts right 16. After even_part (`_mm512_slli_epi32(x, 16)`, kv_cache.hpp:2005-2007@2880c3aa9b) or odd_part (`_mm512_and_epi32(x, hi_16_of_32)`, :2000-2002) the low 16 bits are zero, so the mask never fires and the original bits return.
- The decltype check at :440 is a valid detector: when Row does not declare bf16_chunk, `&Row::bf16_chunk` has type `bf16s (expr<Row,D>::*)(size_t) const noexcept`, not `bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept`, so the comparison distinguishes the inherited fallback. This is the "static_assert" alternative the corrected recommendation allowed ("name the static_assert or the instruction record"). The design places it in the test suite instead of vnni.hpp; that location difference does not change what is detected.
- S15's "[bf16 override detection]" link points at expr.hpp#L110-L117 @2880c3aa9b, the right lines.

The recommendation's replacement text said the fallback "is bit-exact for stored bf16 but adds a shift, NaN check, and narrow per chunk", and the section-8 wording should read "(bit-exact, slower)". Neither :247 nor :440 states that the fallback costs anything (grep of design-r3.txt for "slower", "extra", "round trip" finds only :326, which is about append). Without it, a reader of :440 does not learn why a missing override matters at all. This is one explanatory clause; the actionable guidance (exact signature, decltype check) is correct and complete, so the risk of leaving it out is low.

dispositions.assessment:
The finding said the sentence "Set dma = false" named nothing that exists and gave an imprecise reason. The design now states explicitly that the packed types carry neither a dma template parameter nor a static dma member, and gives the correct reason. The referent problem is gone.

Facts checked in :241:

That alias is instantiated only for matmul operand owner types; no consumer in the design passes a packed view or row there. A future generic reader of `X::dma` would fail to compile loudly, never silently.
- "An arbitrary logical row is not a contiguous DMA input": RIGHT. h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:11-15@2880c3aa9b: the dma parameter means DMA-safe memory, and "Logically, being DMA-safe requires contiguity, namely that the last stride is 1". A pair-interleaved row has stride 2 in bf16 elements.

dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation asked for one sentence stating that the existing generic expression slice already accepts a packed view through its rank-2 expr base, captures it by reference, that only a named lvalue view may be sliced, that the owner must not be passed to slice<> because its Owner& overload forwards a temporary as_view() into that capture, and that the design leaves the path as is with no deleted overload. It also asked to narrow or remove the sentence that could be read as "no slice path exists".

Facts checked against h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp@2880c3aa9b (byte-identical to f46e48bab498):
- "can accept an lvalue packed view": RIGHT. slice.hpp:147-150 `template <typename B, size_t in_d0, size_t in_d1, typename... Offsets> requires(d0 != DYN_SIZE && sizeof...(ds) == 1) auto operator()(expr<B, in_d0, in_d1> const& v_in, ...)`. The design's view inherits expr<view_type,R,D> (:240), so it binds. The lambda indexes `v_in[i + offset0]` and wraps the row in `slice_expr<Row&&, d1>` (slice.hpp:170-174), which needs the row to satisfy `expression` (expr.hpp:141-143 requires `size_`; the rank-1 base defines `static constexpr const size_t size_ = N` at expr.hpp:88) and to provide chunk/bf16_chunk/fp16_chunk (expr.hpp:710-722; fp16_chunk comes from the base at :121-127).
- "It captures that view by reference": RIGHT. slice.hpp:168-169 "// It's critical that `v_in` be captured by reference here. auto f = [=, &v_in](size_t i) {".
- "Do not ... use the owner overload: that overload creates a temporary view internally": RIGHT. slice.hpp:38-42 `template <typename Owner, typename... Offset> requires requires(Owner& owner) { owner.as_view(); } auto operator()(Owner& owner, size_t offset0, Offset... offsets) { return (*this)(owner.as_view(), offset0, offsets...); }`. For a v_vnni_tensor the `as_view()` prvalue is not a view<>/const_view<> or const_views<>, so only the expr const& overload is viable, and the temporary bound to `v_in` dies at the end of that return statement while the lambda still holds `&v_in`.
- "Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged" (:288) is the design's explicit choice of "leave the path as is", which implies no deleted overload is added; "This proposal adds no lifetime guarantee for that existing fallback" says the same from the caller's side.
- The sentence that could be misread as "no slice path exists" was removed rather than narrowed. Removal satisfies the finding's purpose.

Not stated: the generic path's `offset1 % 64 == 0` and `d1 % 64 == 0` rules (slice.hpp:158-161). The design-text-lens correction put them in its suggested sentence; the intent-lens correction said the sentence "could mention" them. No caller at main or in the child slices a cache plane (round-1 F08 evidence), so omitting the rule changes nothing an implementer builds. I treat it as optional and do not carry it as a residual.

SUBSTITUTE ACCEPTED: :440 adds `decltype(&Row::bf16_chunk)` against `bf16s (Row::*)(size_t) const noexcept`. That check distinguishes the inherited base member (whose pointer type is `bf16s (expr<Row,D>::*)(size_t) const noexcept`) from a derived override, so it detects an omitted override at compile time. The round-2 N13 corrected recommendation allowed "the static_assert or the instruction record" as the detector, so I do not demand the objdump region. The fact is right: the rank-2 const_view has a public `explicit const_view(T const* data = nullptr) noexcept` [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:296], and the rank-2 view has `explicit constexpr view(T* data = nullptr) noexcept` [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:43], so const_native_k_view<64,128>{pointer} stays legal and an implicit conversion from a pointer is rejected because the constructor is explicit. A packed V view is a different class template (v_vnni_view), so it cannot convert to const_view either. (2) The verification row now says "Reject implicit raw-pointer arguments" and "Keep explicit native-view pointer construction legal" [design-r3.txt:438]; the word diff shows the OLD text "Reject raw pointers and packed V at native-K kernel calls" was replaced [design-wdiff.txt:1580-1586]. The recommendation's parenthetical "(tests use it)" is not stated; the design's step 6 does not say how t/t_amx_numerics.cpp wraps its raw fixture array `tron::bf16 k[PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128]` passed as `in->k` [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:66, 158-159]. dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation asked for one sentence: the packed append_v_row and load_row overloads and the typed page::set_v/get_v wrappers accept only aligned = true row views, the moved bodies keep their aligned loads and stores, the heterogeneous fixture gains alignas(64), and the claim that section 8 "would flag" an unaligned switch is dropped. The design meets each part.

Checked facts:
- The parameter families carry the literal `true` in the aligned position [design-r3.txt:255], and the text says "The shown alignment flag is true" [design-r3.txt:257]. So the overloads accept only aligned views. The typed wrappers take "the aligned source row" and "an aligned typed destination" [design-r3.txt:268-269].
- "preserve the existing aligned load/store contract" plus "moves today's packed set_v bodies" and "moves today's get_v loops" [design-r3.txt:257-259] keeps the aligned instructions. The bodies use only aligned forms today: `_mm256_load_epi32` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2300, 2308, 2339, 2349], `_mm512_load_ps` [:2380, 2389], `_mm512_store_ps` [:2421, 2430], `_mm256_store_si256` [:2455, 2463].
- "wrapping a pointer does not establish alignment" is right: the rank-1 view constructor stores the pointer with no check [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:125-126].
- The fixture claim is right: `std::array<float, 256> values;` has no alignas and the file contains no alignas at all [t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp@2880c3aa9b:441; git grep alignas finds nothing]; the set_v call is at :443-444. The S16 link "[Source fixture and packed save caller]" points at #L441-L444 [design-r3-links.tsv:211].
- "Source is bf16, fp16, or float. Destination is bf16 or float" matches the set_v overloads [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1622, 1626, 1630] and get_v overloads [:1634, 1639].
- The "would flag" sentence is absent from the design; the instruction-comparison bullets [design-r3.txt:485-489] make no such claim.
- The recommendation's factual clause "today's callers satisfy this" is replaced by the directive "use 64-byte-aligned rows at every migrated call site" [design-r3.txt:257] and the section-9 residual "Verify every migrated caller" [design-r3.txt:519]. The directive is satisfiable: the model passes `&vs[ix][kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size]` [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832] where vs is a kv_buffer_t of tensor storage declared alignas(chunk_alignment) [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:34] and head_size % 32 == 0 is required [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1647]; the GOF callback passes caller scratch documented as 64-byte aligned [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2652-2656; h/tron/gof.hpp@2880c3aa9b:63-64]. A directive to the implementer is at least as strong as the requested factual statement, so I do not count it as missing.
- One verifier suggested naming the `slice<geometry.kv.head_size>()(vs[ix].as_view(), ...)` construction at the model call site. The design says only "Wrap aligned source rows in the packed branch" [design-r3.txt:374]. That was one lens's optional wording, not part of the corrected core recommendation, so it is not a residual.

dispositions.new_defect: Claim: the sentence "Dma preserves the existing contiguous view's DMA flag" [design-r3.txt:257] has nothing to preserve at two of the three migrated call sites, so the implementer must still choose the Dma value there. Evidence: the 16-lane model branch passes a raw pointer `&vs[ix][kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size]` [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832], and the GOF callback passes a raw `bf16* dest` [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2652-2656]; only the 8-lane branch has an existing view, `vs[ix].as_view()` [model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2834-2836], and tensor::as_view() carries dma = false [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:71-72, 35]. The packed bodies do not read the flag, so the choice has no behavioral effect. Recommendation: replace the sentence with "Dma is deduced from the caller's view. Where a call site wraps a raw pointer today (the model's 16-lane branch and the GOF scratch), construct the view with dma = false, the value tensor::as_view() carries."

Checked facts:
- The choice is stated in the accessor table [design-r3.txt:270], in section 4 [design-r3.txt:213], and in step 3 as "Keep the existing 8-lane branch" [design-r3.txt:374]. set_v and get_v rows are labeled "16-lane only" [design-r3.txt:268-269].
- The contradicting sentences are gone. The word diff shows "8-lane forwarding wrapper retains its existing contiguous-row constraints" only as OLD text [design-wdiff.txt:445], "may forward through the unified typed" only as OLD text [design-wdiff.txt:834], and the signature block now lists append_v_row, load_row and copy_token with no row-major forwarding overload [design-r3.txt:255].

In t_llama_unit.cpp the TEST_CASE at :1199-1204 instantiates check_wide_scaled_v<256> and <512>, whose body calls set_v [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:125-142]; the TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE "scaled_v" [:1665-1668] calls set_v at :1723; the non-template TEST_CASE "book.append()" [:2482] calls set_v and get_v at :2533-2539. N29 was a factual error: the count said nine while the round-2 parent list shared ten files with the child. The recommendation offered one fix, replacing the number with "ten" plus the list. The design took a different fix: it removed the count and tells the implementer to remeasure the shared-file set with git diff --name-only against the final parent list (:389). The error is gone, and the replacement instruction is correct and durable.

The removal is the better fix, and I checked why. The round-3 parent step table (:372-377) lists kv_cache_fwd.hpp (new), v_vnni.hpp (new), kv_cache.hpp, model.hpp, self_attention.hpp, amx_attn_iface.hpp, amx_attn.cpp, full.hpp, t_llama_unit.cpp, t_amx_numerics.cpp, t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp and heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp. common.hpp left the parent list in this revision (:319 "Keep token_ix_needed, the page-readiness rule, in common.hpp. Its existing comment is accurate and needs no edit."; :374 "Leave common.hpp 's page-readiness rule unchanged."). The child changes 25 files (`git diff --name-only c7844ca2ce 30c4ac82cb`). The intersection with the round-3 parent list is nine files: kv_cache.hpp, model.hpp, self_attention.hpp, amx_attn_iface.hpp, amx_attn.cpp, full.hpp, t_llama_unit.cpp, t_amx_numerics.cpp, t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp. So the recommended literal text "ten of the same files" would itself be wrong against this revision. A count written into the page goes stale whenever the parent scope moves, which is what the N30 intent-lens correction warned about for dated lists. Removing the number and pointing at the final parent list as the scope to compare resolves the finding without introducing a new stale fact.

The section-9 row (:523) matches the body change (:389); this is not a table-only claim.

dispositions.assessment:
The round-2 sentence "A K token owns separate 4-byte lanes in a shared cache line" is replaced by the recommended wording. The word diff confirms the replacement at this spot (design-wdiff.txt:1451-1454). Every fact in the new sentence checks out against the child source.

- One 4-byte lane holds two consecutive dimensions of one token: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:46-47 ("The two values of one dimension pair share one 32-bit lane") and :15-17.
- One 64-byte line holds that pair for 16 tokens, so sixteen tokens share every line: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:16-17 and :49-51 (BLOCK_TOKENS_16 = 64 bytes / (2 * sizeof(bf16))).
- A 128-dimension token owns 64 such lanes in 64 different lines: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:135-137 ("Only this token's 64 pair slots are written") and h/tron/gof.hpp@30c4ac82cb:69-70 ("a token's 128 values sit in 64 lines").
- Lane scatter: scatter_row = 4 x _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 with DWORD_BYTES_4 scale, k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:139-146. Lane-masked stores: _mm512_mask_storeu_epi32 with the present mask, :211-213. Full-block stores write whole lines (:206-209) without a read-merge-rewrite, so "Never read, merge, and rewrite the whole 64-byte line" stays true.
- Disjoint token lanes across workers: h/tron/models/common.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1060-1061 ("Their writers touch disjoint token lanes").

The verifier's optional clause "of its token block" is not present. The lead's recommendation did not ask for it, and the sentence is correct without it: the 64 lines of a 128-dimension token all lie in the four panels of its token block. The design's index formula at design-r3.txt:209 stays consistent with the sentence. The [S10] link still lands at k_vnni.hpp#L42-L310 (design-r3-links.tsv:172), past the layout comment at lines 1-31; the recommendation did not ask to move it, so this is not a residual.

Facts checked, all at 30c4ac82cb (the child):
- Two overload pairs exist. save_k_helper: operation_ix template form at model.hpp:2952-2959 and descriptor form at :2961-2989. save_k: operation_ix form at :3064-3070 ("size_t n_workers = 1") and descriptor form at :3072-3079. The design's "both existing save_k/save_k_helper overload pairs: the operation-index pair and the descriptor pair" matches.
- The worker-0 duties in the shared case match save_k_impl model.hpp:3009-3058: k_store_cut_units (:3013) and opened.fetch_add (:3017) = window setup; the main thread also claims units (:3018-3023) = block claims; the join loop (:3026-3038); mark_k_complete (:3049); credit_gof_save (:3053); upstream_kvs_ready.count_down (:3058).
- The helper side matches save_k_helper model.hpp:2967-2988: `if constexpr (!k_vnni::layout_on<...>) return;` (:2967), `if (!k_store_shared<geometry>(q_batch, n_workers)) return;` (:2970), the range assert `worker_ix >= 1 && worker_ix < n_workers` (:2973-2975), wait for the window (:2976-2979), claim loop (:2981-2986), finished.fetch_add (:2987), no completion marks. k_store_shared itself checks layout_on (:2807). So "First preserve the existing layout_on and k_store_shared checks" and the two-case description are right.
- The serial case matches: worker 0 calls store_k_block(0, n_items) at :3040 and then the completion loop.
- Generator: run() is Method "run" (TronCpp.hs:1169) and holds n_workers in scope (:1217 calls run_main_help(q_batches, 1 + i, n_workers)); saveKv emits "save_k" with [key, n_workers] (:2405-2408). run_main_help is Method "run_main_help" (:1273) with params worker_ix, n_workers (:1283) and concatenates runHelperStatement (:1281), which emits "save_k_helper" with [key, worker_ix, n_workers] (:2337-2340). So "run() passes 0, n_workers" and "run_main_help passes worker_ix, n_workers" describe the merged shape correctly.
- Test files: LoopyTronSpec.hs:2801-2818 asserts the main call text "q_batch->outer_batch,k,n_workers);" and the helper text "q_batch->outer_batch,k,worker_ix,n_workers);"; :3225-3232 asserts ",k,n_workers);" and ",k,worker_ix,n_workers);" a second time. t_llama_unit.cpp:2772-2784 is the three-thread SECTION calling save_k_helper from std::thread helpers and save_k with N_WORKERS_3. The design names both files.
- "Search all old positional calls, which passed only n_workers": needed, because with save_k(..., worker_ix = 0, n_workers = 1) an old three-argument call save_k(q_batch, ks, N) would compile and bind N to worker_ix (the runtime assert "index below that count" would then fire). The sentence covers this trap.
- bin/ingest-cabal exists at 2880c3aa9b and runs `cabal "$@"` in ingest/ (bin/ingest-cabal:1-5), so "Run bin/ingest-cabal test" runs the Haskell tests locally.
- The three residual guesses named by the intent-lens verifier are all answered: (a) the helper entry points are deleted (:420); (b) the main thread passes 0 (:424); (c) the assert becomes "a positive worker count and an index below that count" (:420).

What is missing: the lead's recommendation said "Run the ingest tests (required 'Test ingest' check)" and the design-text verifier asked to note that the same tests run in CI in the required Test ingest job's "Run Haskell ingest tests" step. The design names only the local command. "ingest" appears only at design-r3.txt:390 and :424; neither section 8 nor the CI-ownership subsection mentions the ingest check. The step exists at gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:235-238 (`nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux."tron-ingest:test:ingest-tests"`), and "Test ingest" is in the required list at README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:76-79 (facts-r3.md:75). An implementer should know that a wrong generated call text blocks the child at a required check, not only at a local run.

Separately, the fix added evidence row S18 whose two generator links carry swapped labels (see new_defect).

design-r3.txt:391: "Define k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, and k_vnni_row for the proposed logical expression reads in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp."

Its named consumer is an ordinary host tensor constructed from a packed-K view in the existing layout suite. A 16-dimension chunk gathers eight 4-byte values across eight cache lines. This is an inspection/test read. Production staging, copies, and scores continue to use bulk row operations or whole-plane arguments. dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation asked the design to state the purpose of the K row expression, name its consumer (with a Child-only verification row), tie it to the reviewer's answer on Q3, say that a chunk read is an 8-dword gather across 8 lines and not a hot-path interface, and drop it together with V's if Q3 is rejected. The design does each of these.

- Purpose: tied to Q3 (design-r3.txt:412 and :97). Q3 derives from the reviewer's review 5270587330, which asks for "a uniform interface based upon `expr`" (github-review.json /comments/comments[2]/body). The lead-level fact that no child reader uses expr on K stays true at 30c4ac82cb (dense and partial QK take the whole plane, staging uses get_k_row, copies use gather_row/scatter_row; facts-r2/facts-r3), and the design now says so at :412 ("Production staging, copies, and scores continue to use bulk row operations or whole-plane arguments") and in the child accessor table at :404-407.
- Consumer: "an ordinary host tensor constructed from a packed-K view in the existing layout suite" (:412). The layout suite is t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp, named at :390 and :416; it exists at 30c4ac82cb (git ls-tree) and is registered unconditionally as a fake-labelled test at t/CMakeLists.txt@30c4ac82cb:618. The Child-only verification row adds the consumer (:443).
- Gather cost: 16 dimensions = 8 dimension pairs; each pair row of a panel is 64 bytes apart (k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:110-111 "The pair rows dp = 0..15 of that panel follow at 64-byte steps", :124-131 pair_row_offsets = 16 dwords apart). So "eight 4-byte values across eight cache lines" is right for the 16-lane chunk. gather_row itself is 4 gathers of 16 dwords (k_vnni.hpp:218-221), consistent with the design's bulk load_row.
- Conditional on Q3: :412 last sentence matches the Q3 "If rejected" column at :97 ("Remove matrix and row expression inheritance from both families"), so K and V are dropped together as the intent-lens verifier asked.
- Required-CI limitation: the required Nix build sets neither TRON_K_VNNI nor TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (no match in nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@30c4ac82cb; facts-r3.md:76 for the AMX flag), and the design states that K-expression coverage in required CI is a child obligation (:414, :467, :524). That is an honest limit, not a residual, because the recommendation did not ask the design to solve required-CI coverage here.

The requirement at :391 is no longer a bare "its row expression": :412 gives its purpose, consumer, cost, and exit condition. No fact in the fix is wrong.

Section 9 is consistent: "K-expression scope follows Q3" [design-r3.txt:524] and "K expression is retained as a named compatibility proposal, not a production need" [design-r3.txt:541]. The design did not have to drop the feature; the recommendation allowed keeping it with a named consumer.

design-r3.txt:479 "Before a campaign on delphi-3bda, source ~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/lib-guard.sh and call campaign_guard_acquire. It refuses a busy CI lease, another active user, a configured blackout, an occupied campaign lock, an existing runtron process, or active rinzler serving. Use --allow-serving only with a flow that stops and restores serving. The lock coordinates this user's campaigns; it does not reserve the host against CI."

design-r3.txt:480 "CI holds the host only when /run/lock/systems-test-ci.lease exists, its state is busy, and its expiry is in the future. Clock windows are advisory. Between long runs, recheck ci_took_dut, the guard for CI, another active user, or a configured blackout. Stop on any of these conditions."

Section 9, design-r3.txt:526 "| N37 N38 | List all guard refusal conditions and platform-specific bench limits. Correct the review claim: local sw-dev-01 bench normally aborts, rather than writing an unknown block. [Design section] | Campaign and whole-host benchmark authorization are separate. No benchmark records were refreshed. |"
dispositions.assessment: The recommendation asked the design to list every campaign_guard_acquire refusal condition, state the --allow-serving rule, say the flock reserves the machine only among this user's sessions, and say that ci_took_dut returns busy for the CI lease, another active user, or a blackout window and that the run must stop in any of those cases. Lines 479-480 do all of this. confirmed.title: scaled_v_expr is not named as a permitted user of detail::v_vnni_access, and its file home was dropped
confirmed.section: 5. Interface design, Internal storage access row (design-r3.txt:249) and page::scaled_v row (:273); 6. Conversions and weighted sums (:329); 7. step 2 (:373); 8. Definition of done (:496)
confirmed.claim: detail::scaled_v_expr is defined inside kv_cache.hpp, which is cache code. Its 16-lane constructor loads whole 64-byte pair tiles with _mm512_load_si512 and feeds them to _mm512_dpbf16_ps. The design gives that constructor a v_vnni_view<const bf16, page_size, head_size>, and the view has no public pointer route (design-r3.txt:248). Line 249 allows detail::v_vnni_access only inside typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels, and says cache callers do not use it. Line 329 says 'Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation' without naming a mechanism. The round-3 edit deleted the round-2 sentence that kept scaled_v_expr in kv_cache.hpp. Reading through row.chunk would double the loads and change the instruction stream that line 329 says to preserve. An implementer cannot tell whether (a) scaled_v_expr counts as a V-specific kernel and may call the friend from kv_cache.hpp, or (b) the weighted-sum body must move into h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp as a typed operation that section 5 does not list. The definition-of-done sentence at :496 cannot be checked until that decision is written.
confirmed.design_quote: Use detail::v_vnni_access , a friend declared with the V types, only inside typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels. The child uses a separate detail::k_vnni_access in its own header. Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers. [...] Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation.

votes.reason: The central claim holds: the design no longer says where detail::scaled_v_expr obtains the packed V address, and its helper rule does not say whether that class may use the friend. Every checkable fact is right. (1) detail::scaled_v_expr is cache code: kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1987-1990 opens namespace detail and the struct, :1992 stores `const bf16s* const data`, and the constructor at :2066-2069 takes a raw `const bf16s* data`. (2) The 16-lane body loads whole 64-byte pair tiles with _mm512_load_si512 and feeds them to _mm512_dpbf16_ps (:2019-2034, :2087-2090, :2102-2109; eight tiles per pair at head_size 128). page::scaled_v passes `kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[0]` at :2260-2261. (3) design-r3.txt:273 gives the 16-lane constructor "a packed read-only V view"; :248 says views expose no public raw-pointer constructor, data member, or pointer conversion; :249 permits detail::v_vnni_access "only inside typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels" and says "Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers"; :329 says "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" and names no mechanism. (4) The v_vnni.hpp operation list at :254 and step 1 at :371 names only append, load, and token copy; no weighted-sum operation is listed. Step 2 at :373 keeps "typed weighted-sum inputs" in kv_cache.hpp. (5) design-wdiff.txt @old 4447 shows the round-2 sentence "Keep typed scaled_v_expr here unless a real include dependency requires a separate header" in the deleted OLD segment with no NEW counterpart; grep of r2-findings.md finds no round-2 recommendation asking for that deletion (N24 only cited the sentence as evidence). (6) :39 defines a kernel as "a specific computation", which does not classify scaled_v_expr either way. (7) Reading through row.chunk (:245, one token's fp32 chunk extracted from the 64-byte pair chunk) would load each pair tile twice and replace the dpbf16 with extraction plus fp32 multiply-add, so it would change the instruction stream that :329 ("unrolled loops, and addition order") and the section-8 objdump comparison at :486 aim to preserve. Severity: minor, not major. Both admissible readings (friend use from kv_cache.hpp, or moving the body to v_vnni.hpp) preserve behavior, and the harmful third reading (row.chunk) is caught by the design's own instruction comparison at :486, which names weighted sums. The fix is one sentence. Major is defensible only if the DoD sentence at :496 must be mechanically checkable without an implementer's judgment call.

What the design does not say is how scaled_v_expr, staying in kv_cache.hpp, obtains the pair-tile address. Owners, views and rows expose no public pointer route [design-r3.txt:248]. The helper detail::v_vnni_access is allowed "only inside typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels", and the same row says "Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers" [design-r3.txt:249]. Line 329 says "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" without naming the helper [design-r3.txt:329]; that sentence is not new, round 2 had it too [evidence/claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:316]. An implementer following the letter of "Cache callers ... do not use these helpers" could conclude that a struct defined in kv_cache.hpp may not call the helper, which leaves no compliant way to load whole 64-byte tiles as today's constructor does [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2066-2109: reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size)) then _mm512_load_si512(tile + k) into _mm512_dpbf16_ps]. votes.reason:
The source facts hold. detail::scaled_v_expr lives in kv_cache.hpp, stores `const bf16s* const data`, and its 16-lane constructor loads whole 64-byte tiles with _mm512_load_si512 into _mm512_dpbf16_ps [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1988-1993, 2066-2109]. page::scaled_v passes kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[0] [same file:2252-2262]. The round-3 edit did delete the round-2 sentence "Keep typed scaled_v_expr here unless a real include dependency requires a separate header" [design-wdiff.txt segment @old 4447].

The central claim is overstated in three places.

(1) "Two access rules conflict" is wrong. Line 249 names the only permitted address route, detail::v_vnni_access, and permits it inside "typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels" [design-r3.txt:249]. Line 329 says the address is obtained "only inside the typed implementation" [design-r3.txt:329]. These are compatible when scaled_v_expr is the V-specific kernel that holds the typed implementation. The Words table defines a kernel as code that "performs a specific computation" [design-r3.txt:39], which scaled_v_expr does. Ben's sketch prescribes exactly this reading: "Physical-address access stays in a small internal helper used by SIMD and AMX implementations" and "kernels extract the pointer once and retain the existing instruction sequence" [github-review.json comments[3] body, lines 152 and 209]. The 16-lane weighted sum is a SIMD implementation.

(2) "An implementer cannot tell whether (a) or (b)" is overstated. The remaining text points to option (a). Step 2, whose file is kv_cache.hpp, says "Apply the accessor table, typed weighted-sum inputs, and explicit fill exception" [design-r3.txt:373]. Section 9 says "Type both weighted-sum constructors" [design-r3.txt:520]. Section 5 and step 1 list only owner, view, row expression, append_v_row, load_row and copy_token as the v_vnni.hpp operations [design-r3.txt:253-259, :371], so no weighted-sum operation is planned there. Reading through row.chunk is already ruled out: line 329 requires "unrolled loops, and addition order" to be preserved, and the section 8 objdump comparison names "weighted sums" as a compared region [design-r3.txt:486]. A public tile route is ruled out by line 248 [design-r3.txt:248].

(3) "The definition-of-done sentence at :496 cannot be checked" is wrong. Under (a) the friend use sits inside a layout-specific kernel; under (b) it sits inside a tensor operation. Both satisfy "Packed physical indexing stays inside tensor operations and layout-specific kernels" [design-r3.txt:496].

Consequence for jhan's goal: none for merge or rebase. Either placement gives the same behavior and the same instruction stream. Ben's sketch sanctions kernel-side friend use. The child does not touch scaled_v_expr, v_data, v_base or weights_times_v: a grep of `git diff c7844ca2ce 30c4ac82cb -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp` for those names returns nothing, although that diff changes 277 lines in those two files.

What survives is one missing clause. The design never names scaled_v_expr as a user of detail::v_vnni_access, and it removed the sentence that fixed its file. An implementer who reads "Cache callers and tests do not use these helpers" [design-r3.txt:249] strictly, and sees that scaled_v_expr is defined in kv_cache.hpp, must infer from :373 and :486 that it is a kernel. One sentence removes that inference. The risk if the sentence is not added is low, so the severity is minor, not major.

Replace "An implementer cannot tell whether (a) or (b)" with "The remaining text points to (a): step 2 places typed weighted-sum inputs under kv_cache.hpp [design-r3.txt:373], section 9 says 'Type both weighted-sum constructors' [:520], and the v_vnni.hpp operation list has no weighted sum [:253-259, :371]; the design should say so in one sentence." Keep recommendation (A) only: add to the page::scaled_v row [design-r3.txt:273] "detail::scaled_v_expr stays in kv_cache.hpp. Its 16-lane constructor obtains the pair-tile base once through detail::v_vnni_access and keeps today's load and dot-product loop. confirmed.lead_note: All three verifiers hold the finding and narrow it: the two rules do not contradict each other, because line 249 forbids the helper to "cache callers" and the design never says whether detail::scaled_v_expr is one. The remaining text points to option A: step 2 keeps the typed weighted-sum inputs under kv_cache.hpp [design-r3.txt:373], the v_vnni.hpp operation list has no weighted sum [:253-259, :372], and section 9 says "Type both weighted-sum constructors" [:520]. The round-2 sentence that kept scaled_v_expr in kv_cache.hpp was deleted without any finding asking for it [design-wdiff.txt @old 4447]. The verifiers graded this minor because the reading is recoverable. I keep major: all three judges name it as the one sentence that must exist before implementation starts, and the PV weighted sum runs on every decode step, so two implementers must not resolve it differently. The fix is one sentence at :273 and :373 plus naming scaled_v_expr at :249.

confirmed.claim: The design states type constraints for the new owners and views (even rows, columns divisible by chunk_size, T is bf16 or const bf16, a 16,384-byte packed-K owner) but never says how they are expressed. confirmed.title: for_each_active_slot visits logical slots, not physical; 'logical alias' is undefined and cannot occur in a fixed layout
confirmed.section: 6. Arena construction without clearing, heterogeneous bullet (design-r3.txt:350)
confirmed.claim: The heterogeneous bullet says for_each_active_slot 'dispatches the physical slot to its compile-time geometry' and ends with a caution about a 'logical alias' that the design never defines. In the code, for_each_active_slot iterates slot indices into kv_slot_specs and keeps only slot < logical_slot_count(); its comment calls these logical slots; callers form the physical offset with kv_storage_offset(slot), as fill_random does. A fixed (heterogeneous) layout maps each logical slot to exactly one physical offset: make_kv_slot_offsets computes one prefix per slot and storage_location reads offsets.values[offset.i]. The only aliasing mechanism in book is storage_view_offset_, set by set_storage_view (the EAGLE view shift), read only in the uniform accessor; EAGLE requires uniform geometry, so it never enters the heterogeneous enumeration. For logical slots the two numbers coincide, so the effect is unchanged, but the bullet opens with 'enumerate physical storage offsets', so a reader may look for a physical-offset loop the helper does not provide, or add a deduplication structure for a case that cannot occur. The alias sentence is carried over from round 2 and no earlier round raised it.

(1) for_each_active_slot enumerates descriptor indices, not physical offsets: for_each_slot_impl expands std::index_sequence<n_slots> and passes kv_slot_specs[slots].geometry (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1236-1240); for_each_active_slot keeps only slot < logical_slot_count() (:1243-1249). The lambda receives a slot index; the caller forms the storage offset itself, as fill_random does with kv_storage_offset(slot) (:1060-1061). The design's phrase 'dispatches the physical slot' (design-r3.txt:350) is therefore loose, and its filter 'storage_location(offset, ...)' uses an 'offset' the bullet never forms. (2) 'logical alias' is undefined: it occurs once in the design (design-r3.txt:350); the Words table defines 'slot' only (design-r3.txt:32), not logical slot, physical slot, or alias; every other 'alias' in the design means a type alias or pointer aliasing (design-r3.txt:99, 267, 518, 529). (3) No alias can occur in the heterogeneous enumeration: make_kv_slot_offsets assigns each slot one prefix in one arena (:651-670); storage_location reads offsets.values[offset.i] and slot_specs[offset.i] (:727-735); heterogeneous_kv_cache is built on fixed_kv_layout with allow_layer_prefix = false (heterogeneous_kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:36-37, kv_cache.hpp:745). The only view shift, storage_view_offset_, is written by set_storage_view/reset_storage_view (:892-902), which assert has_eagle_storage(); EAGLE requires eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0 (:771) and calculate_allocation_sizes rejects it otherwise (:1158-1159). The shift is consumed only by the kv_block accessor that requires(layout_t::uniform_geometry) (:1277-1300) via kv_blocks_alias (:1222-1227); kv_block_at_storage<geometry> (:1309-1335) does not read it. The one many-to-one relation in the code is operations sharing a slot (Note [KV slot retention], :113-115 'Several operations can consume one slot'), and a per-slot loop visits such a slot once, so no deduplication is needed under that reading either. (4) The sentence is carried over: design-revised-text.txt:332 has 'Do not construct the same region again for a logical alias.' verbatim; design-wdiff.txt:1071 shows it as OLD context; grep of r1-findings.md and r2-findings.md for 'logical alias' and 'same region again' finds nothing, and the round-2 M04/N25 texts and corrections (r2-findings.md '### M04', '### N25') never mention it. (4) The permitted routes that remain are real but unnamed: the owner is trivially default-constructible with as_view() & [:238-239], writable element access exists [:245], append_v_row exists [:252-253], and a trivially copyable owner accepts memcpy. (7) The recommendation's facts check out: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions x 2 bytes = 16,384 bytes; today's bf16 set_v body zero-extends and shifts stored bits with no numeric conversion, using aligned loads [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2295-2318], so "the bf16 input path keeps exact bits" is right; an explicit const_native_k_view wrap stays legal [:267]. confirmed.title: Definition of done does not carry the test-cost record refresh
confirmed.section: 8. Definition of done for the parent (design-r3.txt:495-499)
confirmed.claim: The definition of done does not name the required CI checks that must be green on the final commit, does not mention the format and lint gate, does not carry the repository's test-cost refresh obligation, and does not state the PR label state. Each is a repository rule the design cites elsewhere, and each is checkable, so leaving them out lets an implementer declare the parent done while a rule is unmet. The refresh obligation matters because CI's cost-data check only reports missing records, so a stale record for a materially changed t_llama_unit does not fail CI and nothing else forces the refresh.
