confirmed.title: Debug row: 'make BUILD_TYPE=Debug <test>' does not reconfigure an existing gen/, and 'Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo' holds for one path only
confirmed.section: 8. Build configurations table, row 'NaN-preserving Debug check, 16 lanes' (design-r3.txt:455; worktree rule :449)
confirmed.claim: The row tells the agent to run targeted conversion cases with make BUILD_TYPE=Debug and the test target. That command changes the build type only when Make re-runs the CMake configure step, and Make re-runs it only when the gen/config/test stamp is missing or one of its listed inputs changed; none of those inputs tracks BUILD_TYPE. So in a gen/ already configured as RelWithDebInfo, make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit keeps the cached RelWithDebInfo and TRON_IGNORE_NAN stays defined; the agent would test the macro-defined policy while believing it tested the Debug policy. Conversely, in a worktree configured by hand with the row's cmake line, the first plain make target re-runs cmake with Make's default -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo and silently undoes the Debug configuration, while in a Make-configured Debug worktree a later plain make keeps Debug. The sentence 'Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo' is true for the first path and false for the second, and the row does not say which. The t_% Make target also builds and then runs the whole binary with no Catch2 filter. The design's separate-worktree rule (:449) and 'Confirm the macro is absent' limit the damage, so the risk is low.
confirmed.design_quote: Run targeted conversion cases using make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target, or build with cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit after Debug configuration. Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo. Confirm the macro is absent.

So `make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit` in a gen/ that already holds an up-to-date gen/config/test stamp does not reconfigure. A hand-configured gen/ has no gen/config/test stamp, so the first plain make target reconfigures with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo.

Why the finding does not hold against the design text. (1) The failure scenario needs an existing RelWithDebInfo gen/. The design forbids that scenario: "Use a separate worktree for each baseline/head and configuration pair, with the normal gen/ build directory in each" [design-r3.txt:449]. The Debug check is a row of the configuration table [design-r3.txt:455], so it gets its own worktree with a fresh gen/. In a fresh worktree both options of the row give Debug: `make BUILD_TYPE=Debug t_llama_unit` configures with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug because the stamp is missing, and `cmake --build gen --target t_llama_unit` after the row's cmake line keeps the hand configuration. (2) The design already warns that Make may reconfigure gen/: "repository Make targets hardcode gen/ and may reconfigure it. Confirm the cached feature values after invoking them" [design-r3.txt:449], and "Plain Make defaults can restore RelWithDebInfo" [design-r3.txt:455]. The word "can" is accurate for both paths the finding separates. A Make-configured Debug tree also reconfigures to RelWithDebInfo once any configure input changes (a CMakeLists.txt, config/models.yaml, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh, or a stamp) [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:538-543]. So the finding's own sentence "In a Make-configured Debug worktree a later plain make keeps Debug" is only conditionally true, and the design's hedged sentence is the safer statement. (3) The design already requires the check that detects a wrong build type: "Confirm the macro is absent" [design-r3.txt:455] and "Record compiler version, build type, flags, and generated compile definitions" [design-r3.txt:449]. The Bits-and-conversions row selects NaN expectations with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN [design-r3.txt:437], so the test passes under either policy, and the macro check is what proves which policy ran. The design says to do that check. The finding itself says the risk is low for these reasons.

What survives is a note-level wording point, not an ambiguity that changes what gets built: the t_% Make target runs the whole binary with no Catch2 filter [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:886-887], so "Run targeted conversion cases using make BUILD_TYPE=Debug with the applicable test target" [design-r3.txt:455] cannot run a subset of cases by itself. The agent must run gen/t_llama_unit with a case-name argument after building. Also the design does not name where to confirm the build type and the macro. Neither point misleads an implementer into building the wrong thing.

(3) All 15 test call sites pass raw pointers or `.data()` of arrays and tensors [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:107, 1723, 1923, 2038, 2533-2539, 2568-2569, 2690, 2705, 2721, 2761, 2792, 2802, 2824; t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp@2880c3aa9b:443-444]. The child section repeats the rule for K: "The boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties" [design-r3.txt:405]. Round-2 N15 asked for exactly this form, with a lowercase, free "dma" parameter [r2-findings.md, N15 RECOMMENDATION and both verifier corrections]. Model site: the finding's "nothing to preserve" is wrong. The 16-lane branch passes a raw pointer today [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832]. That pointer is into a stack array, alignas(64) std::array<bf16, ...> v_scratch [src/tron/gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203, :213; h/tron/gof.hpp@2880c3aa9b:62-66]. No view exists there. confirmed.title: Uniform-array rule: the 'existing uniform accessor' justification holds only for uniform reclaimability
confirmed.section: 6. Arena construction without clearing, uniform bullet (design-r3.txt:349)
confirmed.claim: The uniform bullet justifies the one-array rule by 'the existing uniform accessor's indexing across slots'. Facts confirmed. The uniform accessor kv_block() has two branches. The uniform_reclaimability branch indexes one kv_block_t array from kv_blocks_alias across slots [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1284-1289]. The else branch addresses each physical slot through slot_base [:1290-1299]. It places the construction helper inside book::allocate_kv_group "after installing a successful allocation" and says "Both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use this path" [design-r3.txt:348]. allocate_kv_group runs once per arena: retained then reclaimable in the constructor [:1101-1102] and reclaimable in restore [:968]. That is one array per arena, for every allocate_kv_group call. The two-arena mixed-retention layout is covered without a special case. (2) The design never names kv_blocks_alias: 0 hits in design-r3.txt and 0 hits in the HTML. Its placeholder region_base is "the selected region's aligned address" [design-r3.txt:342], and inside allocate_kv_group the arena just installed is the only region at hand [kv_cache.hpp:1202-1206]. So the recommendation's "not kv_blocks_alias" corrects a pointer the design does not give. (3) The justification sentence remains true in substance for the else branch. slot_base returns arena + n_pages * byte_offset [:1188-1197], and byte_offset is the sum of the preceding same-arena slots' bytes [:659-661]. Under uniform geometry every slot has the same kv_block_t, so slot_base lands at block index (within-arena slot ordinal * n_kv_heads) * n_pages, and the accessor adds kv_head * n_pages + pg [:1298]. Every block the accessor reaches is an element of the per-arena array the design constructs. sizeof(kv_block_t) equals the per-page block byte count [:1316-1318], so the arena byte count is an integer multiple of it.

confirmed.section: 7. Child interface table, Copy and score readers row (design-r3.txt:407); compare 5. One cache row-write rule (:261); 8. Child only row (:443); 9. row N03.. (:514)
confirmed.claim: For V the design says a defaulted same-type owner copy is sufficient when a whole owner must be copied and forbids a copy_plane operation. confirmed.title: Deduction trap for typed K row arguments not restated for the child's callers
confirmed.section: 7. Child interface table, page::set_k_row / page::get_k_row row (design-r3.txt:405)
confirmed.claim: The K row parameters are given as const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> with Aligned and Dma as template parameters. Template argument deduction does not consider conversions, so a writable view or a raw pointer at the call site does not bind. Every child caller passes one of those: store_k_block passes the slice view's raw .data or a stack array, the FPGA callback passes a raw scratch pointer, and the layout test passes row.data(). Section 5 states the explicit-construction rule for the V rows only (:257). The K row does not repeat it.
confirmed.design_quote: Use const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for save and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for load. The boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties.

votes.reason: The central fact holds. The rank-1 view is a final struct that derives only from expr<view<...>, d0> [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:116-117]. The rank-1 const_view is a separate final template [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:361-362]. Its writable-to-read-only conversion is a converting constructor [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:382, 385], and its raw-pointer constructor is explicit [view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:373]. Template argument deduction does not use converting constructors, and there is no derived-to-base path from view to const_view. So a parameter of type const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> cannot deduce Aligned or Dma from a writable view or from a bf16 pointer. The child's callers all pass raw pointers or a writable view's pointer: model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2861-2864 (row_of = slice of ks[ix].as_view(); ks is a non-const kv_buffer_t& at :2857 and a non-const as_view() returns a writable view [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:71]), :2920 (kout.data), :2883 and :2924 (alignas(64) bf16 conv[16][head_size], conv[0]), full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2645 and :2655 (bf16* dest), t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cb:401 and :405 (row.data(), got.data()). The design states the explicit-construction rule only in the V row-write bullets of section 5 [design-r3.txt:257; section 5 spans lines 228-293]. The K row [design-r3.txt:405] says the boolean template arguments "preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties" and "Wrap scratch without copying" but never states that a writable view or a raw pointer does not bind. A grep for "deduc" in design-r3.txt hits only line 257. Severity: the compiler rejects each unwrapped call and the fix is local, so an implementer would not build the wrong thing. The design makes h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp include h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp, and the child makes h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp include h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. Both are kernels-to-tensor includes. Precedent exists: dotter.hpp, expr.hpp, strided_copy.hpp and topk.hpp already include tensor headers. The design does not cite the precedent. It also places a header named after the KV cache in a directory the README describes as hardware-agnostic tensor facilities. A reviewer who checks the README can reject the placement; the page gives the implementer no answer.
confirmed.design_quote: amx_attn_iface.hpp includes kv_cache_fwd.hpp and remains free of intrinsics.
confirmed.evidence: README.code-org.md@2880c3aa9b:55 ('tron/tensor | Hardware-agnostic and on-CPU tensor facilities'), :58 ('Dependencies (aspirational)'), :76 ('tron/kernels depends on tron/simd'), :78 ('tron/tensor depends on tron/simd, tron/kernels'). Existing kernels-to-tensor includes at 2880c3aa9b: h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp:10 (tron/tensor/view.hpp), expr.hpp:13 (tron/tensor/seq.hpp), strided_copy.hpp:4 and topk.hpp:16 (tron/tensor/array_like.hpp).
confirmed.recommendation: After design-r3.txt:284 add: 'This kernels-to-tensor include follows the existing dotter.hpp:10 and expr.hpp:13 precedent. README.code-org.md:76-78 lists the opposite direction as aspirational; state the precedent in the parent PR description.' Optionally rename the header to something layout-oriented, such as h/tron/tensor/kv_views_fwd.hpp, so the tensor directory does not carry a models-layer name.

votes.reason: Central claim confirmed against primary sources. (1) The design specifies two kernels-to-tensor includes: "amx_attn_iface.hpp includes kv_cache_fwd.hpp" [design-r3.txt:284] where the header lives at h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp [design-r3.txt:232, :372], and "h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header" (the K tensor header h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp) [design-r3.txt:391-392]. (2) README.code-org.md@2880c3aa9b (byte-identical at live main 1400fa4481) says "tron/tensor | Hardware-agnostic and on-CPU tensor facilities" [:55], "Dependencies (aspirational)" [:58], "tron/kernels depends on tron/simd" [:76], "tron/tensor depends on tron/simd, tron/kernels" [:78]. All four cited lines are exact. (3) The precedent exists exactly as cited: h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp:10 includes tron/tensor/view.hpp, expr.hpp:13 includes tron/tensor/seq.hpp, strided_copy.hpp:4 and topk.hpp:16 include tron/tensor/array_like.hpp; these are the only four kernels-to-tensor includes at 2880c3aa9b and at 30c4ac82cb. (4) The design text has zero occurrences of "code-org", "aspirational", "precedent", "dotter.hpp" or "expr.hpp", so it cites neither the README nor the precedent. Rounds 1 and 2 never raised directory placement (no hits in r1-findings.md or r2-findings.md), so this is new, not a regression. The related id F43 is right: r1-findings.md:521 "Typed kernel parameters pull SIMD headers into intrinsics-free header" is the header-boundary finding whose round-2 fix ("share a small intrinsics-free declarations header", round-2 text line 272) round 3 turned into kv_cache_fwd.hpp. G16 and G17 do not appear anywhere in the scratchpad and could not be verified. One detail is wrong (see correction): the child at 30c4ac82cb does not include any tensor header from h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp. Severity stays at note: the README list is explicitly "aspirational"; AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:113 says to read README.code-org.md "only as needed"; no tool enforces the direction (.iwyu_mappings.imp maps symbols to headers; the "dependency" hits in GNUmakefile:729 and bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh are CI pin checks); and the documented tensor-to-kernels direction also exists in practice (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:21 and views.hpp:6 include tron/kernels/expr.hpp, view.hpp:6 includes tron/kernels/chunky.hpp), so the two directories are already mutually dependent. Ben's own straw-man comment places the layout and view types at "// h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp" [evidence/github-review.json, Ben's sketch section 1], so the h/tron/tensor/ directory follows the reviewing maintainer's suggestion and the rejection risk the finding describes is low.
votes.correction: Three corrections. (a) Attribution: replace "the child makes h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp include h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp" with "the design's child-port plan makes h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp include h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp [design-r3.txt:391-392]". At 30c4ac82cb h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp does not exist, and the child's h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:32-40 includes only <cstddef>, <cstdint>, <cstring>, <immintrin.h>, <type_traits>, common/attributes.hpp, common/numerics/bf16.hpp and common/numerics/fp16.hpp. (b) Narrow the risk sentence: the README list is labeled "aspirational" [README.code-org.md@2880c3aa9b:58], AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:113 says to read it "only as needed", no tool enforces it, and tensor headers already include kernels headers (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:21, view.hpp:6, views.hpp:6 @2880c3aa9b), so the directories are mutually dependent today. Add: Ben's sketch itself places the layout and view types under h/tron/tensor/ ("// h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp", evidence/github-review.json, Ben's straw-man section 1), so only the header NAME kv_cache_fwd.hpp (after h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp [design-r3.txt:373]) departs from his layout-oriented naming; the optional rename recommendation should cite that. (c) relates_to: keep F43 (r1-findings.md:521); drop or re-verify G16 and G17, which are absent from the scratchpad. The recommendation text can stand with the corrected attribution; suggested sentence after design-r3.txt:284: "This kernels-to-tensor include follows the existing includes at h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp:10 and expr.hpp:13 (2880c3aa9b). README.code-org.md:76-78 lists the opposite direction under 'Dependencies (aspirational)'; tensor headers already include kernels headers (view.hpp:6, views.hpp:6). State the precedent in the parent PR description."

votes.reason:
The central claim holds. The design text never mentions README.code-org.md, the documented dependency direction, or the existing precedent. A grep of design-r3.txt for "code-org", "aspirational", "precedent", "kernels-to-tensor" and "dependency direction" returns zero hits. The design also gives no rationale for placing the new headers under h/tron/tensor; it only names the paths [design-r3.txt:232, 258, 372, 391].

The finding's source facts are right. README.code-org.md@2880c3aa9b:55 describes tron/tensor as "Hardware-agnostic and on-CPU tensor facilities". Line 58 is headed "Dependencies (aspirational)". Line 76 says "tron/kernels depends on tron/simd". Line 78 says "tron/tensor depends on tron/simd, tron/kernels". The four existing kernels-to-tensor includes exist at 2880c3aa9b: h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp:10 (tron/tensor/view.hpp), expr.hpp:13 (tron/tensor/seq.hpp), strided_copy.hpp:4 and topk.hpp:16 (tron/tensor/array_like.hpp).

The design does add two kernels-to-tensor includes. Section 5 says "amx_attn_iface.hpp includes kv_cache_fwd.hpp" [design-r3.txt:284]. Section 7 says "h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes that header", where "that header" is h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp [design-r3.txt:391-392].

This is not a re-raise. Neither r1-findings.md nor r2-findings.md mentions README.code-org.md (0 hits in each).

Severity stays at note for four reasons. (1) The README labels the dependency list "aspirational" [README.code-org.md@2880c3aa9b:58]. (2) Four kernels headers already include tensor headers, so the direction is already reversed in main. (3) Nothing enforces the direction. Only README.md:16 and AGENTS.md:113 reference README.code-org.md at 2880c3aa9b, and AGENTS.md:113-114 says to read it "only as needed". No script or lint checks the submodule graph. (4) The reviewing maintainer's own sketch places the new header at h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp [evidence/github-review.json, comment 5765866077]. An implementer would not build the wrong thing, and the parent PR could still merge.
votes.correction:
Three corrections narrow the finding.

1. Fix the attribution of the K include. The finding says "the child makes h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp include h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp". That is wrong. At 30c4ac82cb the child's h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes only <cstddef>, <cstdint>, <cstring>, <immintrin.h>, <type_traits>, common/attributes.hpp, common/numerics/bf16.hpp and common/numerics/fp16.hpp [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:32-40]. The child has no h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp at all (git ls-tree of h/tron/tensor/ at 30c4ac82cb shows no vnni file). The include is the design's child-adaptation plan [design-r3.txt:392]. Reword to: "the design's child adaptation makes h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp include h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp".

2. Weaken "A reviewer who checks the README can reject the placement". The reviewing maintainer's sketch itself names the path "h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp" [evidence/github-review.json, comment 5765866077]. So the h/tron/tensor directory follows the reviewer's own proposal. The design does not cite the sketch for the directory choice either (grep for "sketch" in design-r3.txt hits lines 46, 69, 71, 76, 96, 97, 213, 539, none about the header path). Reword the risk to: "The page states neither the reviewer's sketch nor the existing four-header precedent as the reason for the placement and the include direction."

3. Adjust the recommendation. After design-r3.txt:284 add one sentence: "This kernels-to-tensor include follows the existing dotter.hpp:10, expr.hpp:13, strided_copy.hpp:4 and topk.hpp:16 includes; README.code-org.md:58-78 lists the opposite direction as aspirational, and the reviewer's sketch places the header under h/tron/tensor." Keep the header rename optional. The "models-layer name" remark is accurate: kv_cache.hpp lives at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp at 2880c3aa9b.

votes.reason:
The factual core holds; the consequence does not, so the finding stays at note and needs narrowing.

Facts confirmed:
- README.code-org.md@2880c3aa9b:55 reads "tron/tensor | Hardware-agnostic and on-CPU tensor facilities". Line 58 reads "Dependencies (aspirational)". Line 76 reads "tron/kernels depends on tron/simd". Line 78 reads "tron/tensor depends on tron/simd, tron/kernels". The file is unchanged at 1400fa4481 and at 30c4ac82cb (git diff --stat prints nothing).
- The design puts the declarations header in h/tron/tensor [design-r3.txt:232, :372] and makes amx_attn_iface.hpp (a h/tron/kernels header) include it [design-r3.txt:284]. The child step makes h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp include h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp [design-r3.txt:392]. Both are kernels-to-tensor includes.
- Precedent exists at 2880c3aa9b: h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp:10 (tron/tensor/view.hpp), expr.hpp:13 (tron/tensor/seq.hpp), strided_copy.hpp:4 and topk.hpp:16 (tron/tensor/array_like.hpp). The design never mentions README.code-org.md or this precedent (grep for "code-org" and "aspirational" in design-r3.txt returns nothing).

Why the consequence is small:
- Ben's own API sketch places the layout and view header at "// h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp" and types the kernel declarations with those views ("Kernel signatures state precisely what they accept: ... weights_times_v_128x4(packed_v_page v, ...)") [github-review.json comments[3]]. So the reviewing maintainer proposed a tensor-directory header consumed by kernel declarations. The sentence "A reviewer who checks the README can reject the placement" contradicts Ben's stated wish.
- The README graph is labeled "aspirational" [README.code-org.md@2880c3aa9b:58]. Live code already breaks it in both directions: tensor headers include kernel headers at h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:21 (tron/kernels/expr.hpp), view.hpp:6 (tron/kernels/chunky.hpp) and views.hpp:6 (tron/kernels/expr.hpp)@2880c3aa9b. The new include adds no new class of violation.
- No repository check enforces the graph. git grep for "code-org" and "deps-tron-submodules" at 2880c3aa9b finds only two reading pointers (AGENTS.md:113 "read README.code-org.md ... only as needed"; README.md:16).
- The include is what the earlier review asked for. Round-2 N14's recommendation reads "a small intrinsics-free declarations header ... amx_attn_iface.hpp includes that header" [r2-findings.md, N14 RECOMMENDATION]. Round-1 F43's verifier corrections said including a tensor header keeps the header's documented contract [r1-findings.md, F43]. The design's section 9 records both [design-r3.txt:518, :550].
- The header name kv_cache_fwd.hpp inside h/tron/tensor is a naming choice with no effect on compilation or on Ben's acceptance. Ben's sketch used vnni.hpp; the design's v_vnni.hpp and k_vnni.hpp already parallel that name.

An implementer builds the right thing either way, and the parent PR's mergeability does not depend on this sentence. That is a note, not a change the design must make.

confirmed.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3 at note. Corrections: at 30c4ac82cb the child's h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp includes no tensor header; the include is the design's plan. rejected.title: Writable element access has no caller, yet drives Q2 and three write rules
rejected.section: 5. Interface design, operation table (design-r3.txt:245); Words (:54); Q2 (:96); 6. write table and bullet (:315, :317); 8. Typed function boundaries (:438)
rejected.claim: No code at main writes a single packed-V element. Every V write goes through set_v, append_v, or the layout-blind fill, including the tests that plant NaN poison. The parent still makes matrix[token][dimension] writable when T is bf16. That third write path forces the design to add a 'Direct element update' row, a readiness caveat, a 'must not replace cache append' rule, a const-row-mutation compile check, and the Q2 const debate. The Words table says the row type 'reads' a logical row. Read-only element access in the parent removes all of that with no caller lost. Note for the verifier: this sits next to the rejected F09 (generic expression writes) and N21 (at() as a second spelling); the finder states it covers scalar element writes, which F09 did not, and keeps at().
rejected.design_quote: Writable access changes only that element. A const matrix returns a read-only row. A const row returns a read-only element, even when its element type is bf16 .
rejected.evidence: Production V writes: model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832 (set_v) and kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1943-1946 (append_v inside copy_storage_slot). Test V writes including NaN poison use set_v: t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1920-1923, :2702-2705, :2789-2792, :142, :796, :1554, :1723, :2533-2569. rejected.recommendation: In the operation table (design-r3.txt:245) replace 'Writable access changes only that element.' with: 'Element access is read-only for both element types in the parent: operator[] and at() return the stored bf16 by value. No caller at main writes a single V element; all writes use append_v_row or copy_token. Add writable at() only when a caller needs it.' votes.reason:
Short version: the finding's fact is right, its conclusion is not. No code at main writes a single packed-V element. But the writable element access the finding wants removed is the reviewer's own `T& at()`, so removing it is a departure from the sketch, and the finding does not say so. That is the same reason round-1 F09 was rejected.

Fact check (holds). Every `.v[` access in h/, src/ and t/ at 2880c3aa9b sits inside kv_cache.hpp bodies: set_v (2296, 2335, 2376), get_v (2414, 2448), append_v (1880, 1882), the 8-lane token copy (1952, 1954), the 8-lane v()/v_ptr() accessors (1677-1722) and scaled_v (2261) [git grep '\.v\[' 2880c3aa9b -- h/ src/ t/]. page::v_data (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1609) and kv_block::v_base (:2237) return const pointers. The production writes are model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831-2832 (set_v) and kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1944-1946 (append_v inside copy_storage_slot). Every test V write uses set_v (t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:142, 796, 1554, 1723, 1923, 2533-2535, 2568-2569, 2690, 2705, 2721, 2792, 2802; t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:443; t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:98) or book::fill_random (t_llama_unit.cpp:784-785, 2008). The NaN poison at 1918-1923, 2700-2705 and 2788-2792 goes through set_v. So "writable element access has no caller at main" is true.

Why the conclusion fails. Ben's sketch declares `T& at(size_t token, size_t dim) const noexcept` on vnni_view<T, Layout> and says "at() is useful for inspection and scalar access; hot paths use the bulk operations" [evidence/github-review.json comments[3], section 2 of the sketch]. With T = bf16 that returns a writable reference. The design's "Writable access changes only that element" (design-r3.txt:245) is that same operation in the rank-2 spelling the design chose under Q3 (design-r3.txt:98). The finding quotes Ben's sentence but omits the `T&` signature. The round-1 scope table already listed "view[token][dim] element access with asserts [Ben's at()]" under KEEP [r1-findings.md:51]. Round-1 F09 was refuted because "the recommendation removes exactly the operations Ben asked for, and the finding does not say so" [r1-findings.md:632]. G11 has the same defect. "No caller" alone does not show that a reviewer-requested operation is wrong.

The "drives Q2" claim is wrong. Q2 exists to resolve round-1 F02 and F04, both major, which asked the design to state the const rule and flag the departure from Ben's std::span statement [r1-findings.md:15-33]; F04 is graded resolved [r2-findings.md:1029]. Q2, the "Direct element update" row, the "must not replace cache append" sentence and the "const-row mutation" check were all in the round-2 text [evidence/claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:83, 218-219, 301, 303, 397]. Round 3 changed only "Non-const writable" to "Writable" and "yields" to "returns" [design-wdiff.txt:565-572]. So the text is not new, and its purpose is the const contract Ben himself stated ("As with std::span, a const view object does not make its elements const"), not a side effect of writable access.

Severity if the finding held as written: minor. What survives: a note-level wording mismatch (see correction).
votes.correction: Narrow the finding to one wording mismatch, note level, no design change to the interface: the Words row "v_vnni_row reads one logical row" (design-r3.txt:54) does not match the operation table, where a non-const v_vnni_row<bf16, D> returns a writable element (design-r3.txt:245, "Writable access changes only that element", and :243, "Restrict T to bf16 or const bf16"). Recommended text for design-r3.txt:54: "v_vnni_row accesses one logical row; it is writable only when its element type is bf16." Optionally add one sentence after design-r3.txt:317: "No caller at main writes a single V element; writable element access exists for the reviewer's scalar at() and for fixtures." Drop the recommendation to make element access read-only, drop the deletion of the "Direct element update" row (:315), the fixture sentence (:317) and the "const-row mutation" check (:438), and drop the Q2 rewrite (:96): Ben's sketch declares `T& at(size_t token, size_t dim) const noexcept` [github-review.json comments[3]], and Q2 resolves round-1 F02/F04 [r1-findings.md:15-33; r2-findings.md:1029]. Fix the evidence line: cite Ben's `T& at(...)` declaration, not only his prose sentence.

votes.reason:
Short version: the code facts in G11 hold, but the recommendation removes an operation the reviewer's own sketch specifies, and the design already bounds that operation with the rules G11 wants deleted. The finding is a scope disagreement with a flagged, sketch-derived choice, not an omission, error, or contradiction in the design text.

What I confirmed from the finding's evidence:
- No code at main writes one packed-V element by hand. Every `.v[` access at 2880c3aa9b is inside kv_cache.hpp: set_v (2296, 2335, 2376), get_v (2414, 2448), v/v_ptr (1681-1716), append_v (1880-1882), copy_storage_slot (1952-1954), scaled_v (2261) [git grep at 2880c3aa9b, h/ src/ t/]. kv_cache.hpp is byte-identical at live main 1400fa4481 [facts-r3.md:42-43].
- The NaN-poison tests use set_v [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1920-1923, 2702-2705, 2789-2792]. The finder's citation of these lines is right.
- The expression consumer the design names (host tensor construction) reads rows via rhs[i] and chunk(i) [tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:274-280, 83]. It does not need a writable element. So a read-only element would be technically feasible.

Why the finding is refuted:
1. The reviewer's sketch specifies writable scalar access. Its view has `T& at(size_t token, size_t dim) const noexcept { ... return data_[Layout::offset(token, dim)]; }` [evidence/github-review.json, .comments.comments[3].body, section "2. A view carries layout and constness"]. With T = bf16 that reference is writable. The sketch then says "at() is useful for inspection and scalar access" and "As with std::span, a const view object does not make its elements const. vnni_view<const bf16, Layout> does." The finder quotes the first sentence but omits the `T&` return type. Writable element access is therefore the sketch's choice, not an addition by the design.
2. Removing it would be an unflagged departure from the sketch. Round-1 F02 established that departures from the sketch must be recorded as reviewer questions [r1-findings.md:15-24]. The design's Q2 exists to flag the one departure it does make: const view objects block mutation, unlike the sketch's std::span rule [design-r3.txt:96, :101]. The finding's rewritten Q2 ("Is read-only element access sufficient for the parent? Proposed: yes") would adopt a second, larger departure by default. Under the same rule it would need a reviewer question, not a unilateral simplification.
3. The "no caller" argument was already weighed in round 1. F09 argued that generic write paths into packed V have no caller and was rejected because the reviewer asked for those operations [r1-findings.md:627-632]. The argument is weaker here: the sketch's own code contains the writable at(). The finder correctly notes G11 differs from F09 (scalar, not expression writes) and from N21 (writability, not spelling), but supplies no new evidence that the sketch's writable at() is wrong.
4. The design already bounds the third write path. "Direct element update ... does not establish cache readiness" [design-r3.txt:315]; "Direct element mutation is useful for fixtures; it must not replace cache append" [:317]; "Direct element writes do not establish readiness" at the comment sites [:362]. These are the guards an implementer needs. G11 calls them cost; they are the design stating the hazard and the rule.
5. Nothing here is new in round 3. The writable-element row, the "Direct element update" row, the fixtures sentence, and the const-row mutation check all existed in the round-2 text [evidence/claude-review-r2/design-revised-text.txt:218-219, 301, 303, 397]. Round 2 raised N21 (at() spelling) and rejected it; no round-2 finding disputed writability. G11 re-litigates an accepted choice.

What survives (note level, no removal): the Words row says "v_vnni_row reads one logical row" [design-r3.txt:54] while the operation table gives that row writable element access when T is bf16 [:245]. This is a wording slip, not a contradiction an implementer would act on, because :245 is the normative row.

That call takes the odd branch of page::set_v [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2304-2318]. The odd branch loads the pair with _mm512_load_si512 [:2312], merges with _mm512_ternarylogic_epi32 [:2314-2315], and stores [:2316]. It checks no precondition. The finding's factual reading of both sections is right, but its central claim (a contradiction that could make an implementer lose the dirty-buffer case) does not hold.

What the design says. Section 6 gives the precondition twice: "Odd cache append | Yes, pair must be initialized | Even row is preserved" [design-r3.txt:314] and "append of an odd token requires the even partner to have been initialized" [design-r3.txt:353]. Section 5 says the same: "An odd destination merges into the initialized pair" [design-r3.txt:258]. Section 8 says: "Retain scaled_v padding NaN. Poison the odd row, append its even partner through the page::set_v called by save_v_impl, then compute a weighted sum with live count 1 token" [design-r3.txt:436].

Why the contradiction is not there. The finding assumes "Poisoning the odd row is itself an odd cache append". The design does not say how the test applies the poison. The same section-6 table offers a fixture path that needs no initialized pair: "Direct element update | No read of other elements required | Other elements unchanged; this does not establish cache readiness" [design-r3.txt:315], and the bullet under it says "Direct element mutation is useful for fixtures; it must not replace cache append" [design-r3.txt:317]. The design also keeps the layout-blind whole-block poison fill (book::fill_random, fill_storage_slot) as an explicit test-support exception [design-r3.txt:274] and lists "poison fill" among the retained lifecycle cases [design-r3.txt:441]. An implementer who poisons the odd row by a direct element write or by fill_random satisfies both the section-6 precondition and the section-8 order. So section 6 "alone" is exactly where the fixture exception lives.

Why the stated risk does not follow. Section 8 fixes the order: poison, then even append, then weighted sum with live count 1 token [design-r3.txt:436]. The only reordering that also satisfies "pair initialized" is to add an even append BEFORE the poison. The poison is then still present when the tested even append runs, so the dirty-buffer case (an even append clears an odd row that holds NaN) is still exercised. The design's own figure draws exactly this: "Reused pair: Old even row, Odd row: NaN poison -> Append even token -> Append odd token" [design-r3.txt:300-306]. No reordering that follows section 8 loses the case.

Source facts confirmed. The odd set_v path loads the pair, merges the odd half in, and stores, with no precondition check [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2305-2318 (bf16), :2380-2394 (float)]. The retained SECTION "single-token dirty-buffer reuse" builds a fresh book_t bk(1) and poisons slot 1 with p->set_v(..., 1, nan_buf) before any even write, then writes slot 0 with set_v [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:2779-2802]. So the retained test does perform an odd cache append into a never-written pair, and its merged even half is indeterminate until set_v(even) overwrites the pair. That is the only residual: the retained test does not follow the "pair must be initialized" wording, and the design does not say that this fixture use is acceptable. This is a one-clause clarity item, not an error or a contradiction that would change what gets built.
votes.correction: Narrow the finding from "contradiction" to "optional clarification". Drop the claim that poisoning is necessarily an odd cache append (the design sanctions direct element writes and fill_random for fixtures [design-r3.txt:274, :315, :317]) and drop the claim that an implementer could lose the dirty-buffer case (section 8 fixes the order [design-r3.txt:436]). A fixture may poison an odd row of an unwritten pair by an odd append or a direct element write; the merged even half is then indeterminate until the even append overwrites the pair, which is what the retained single-token dirty-buffer reuse case checks." votes.reason:
The central claim is a contradiction between the odd-append precondition and the recommended test order. I could not confirm it.

Facts I confirmed. The design says an odd cache append reads the pair and needs it initialized [design-r3.txt:314, :353, :258]. The design's test row says "Retain scaled_v padding NaN. Poison the odd row, append its even partner through the page::set_v called by save_v_impl, then compute a weighted sum with live count 1 token" [design-r3.txt:436]. The existing test poisons slot 1 with set_v into a fresh book and then writes slot 0 with set_v [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:2779-2802]. The fresh arena comes from try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite, which does no clearing for a trivially constructible element type [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1202; h/system/memory.hpp@2880c3aa9b:323-337]. The odd set_v path loads the pair with _mm512_load_si512 and merges, with no precondition check [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2305-2316]. So the existing poison step does read an unwritten even half. That part of the finding is right.

Why the contradiction does not hold. The design does not say the poison step must be an odd cache append. The same table has a third row, "Direct element update", which reads no other elements and needs no initialized pair [design-r3.txt:315]. The bullet under the table says "Direct element mutation is useful for fixtures; it must not replace cache append" [design-r3.txt:317]. A fixture that poisons by direct element write, then appends the even partner through page::set_v, satisfies the precondition and the recommended order at the same time. The design also states that element storage stays uninitialized until written [design-r3.txt:346], so it already accepts that fixtures touch unwritten storage. The "pair must be initialized" cell is a production readiness rule for the pair's result. The poison step does not aim at a correct pair, so the rule does not apply to it.

Why the consequence is nil. The recommended order came from the round-1 review itself: F01 asked for "poison an odd row, write the even partner through the same page method that save_v_impl calls, then check scaled_v with count = 1" [r1-findings.md:9]. Any reorder that keeps one even append after the poison still covers the dirty-buffer case. A reorder that puts the poison after the last even append makes the weighted sum read NaN, and REQUIRE_FALSE(std::isnan(...)) fails loudly [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:2812-2822]. No silent loss of coverage is possible. An implementer cannot build the wrong parent PR from this text, and Ben's acceptance does not depend on it.

Residue. The retained existing test performs one odd set_v on an unwritten pair. The design's literal precondition does not carve out that fixture step. An optional one-clause note would remove the strict reading. That is a note, not a change the design must make.

findings_intro: Ten finders read the second revision through one lens each (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben and jhan, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs, a regression hunt over the round-2 to round-3 word diff, and a section-9 honesty audit). questions_intro: Design section 2 now carries a decision record: four questions for Ben (Q1 to Q4) with a proposed choice, a fallback if rejected and a record status, plus D5, the native-K typing scope that jhan requested. The owner is the issue assignee, the record place is the parent PR description, and implementation may start on the proposed choices labelled Proposed. All three judges found the record adequate. The table gives my reading of each row against Ben's three comments (evidence/github-review.json) and jhan's request.
questions_rows: Q1. May each concrete view contain its address formula? Proposed: yes; one view per layout, separate V and K owners, no layout-policy template.
Ben's sketch sections 1 and 2 (layout as a template argument of owner and view) and his own reservation: "I'm not entirely convinced of the necessity of separate k_vnni_layout from vnni_view".

Adequate. The proposed choice follows Ben's stated doubt, and the fallback is the sketch itself, so either answer is implementable. The design also confirms jhan's reading of that reservation (design-r3.txt:71); N11 asks it to state what the reading was.
Q2. Should const matrix and row objects prevent element mutation? Proposed: yes at both ranks, following tron's rank-2 view rule.
Ben's sketch: "As with std::span, a const view object does not make its elements const. vnni_view<const bf16, Layout> does."

Adequate, and the question most likely to be answered no, because Ben stated the opposite rule in writing. The design flags the departure and gives a fallback. Keep the const contracts in one table row so a flip is one edit, and settle the row-conversion clause first (N20, G40).
Q3. May packed views expose logical rows through operator[]? Proposed: yes, returning a logical row expression with no public pointer; keep bounds-checked at().
Ben's review asked for the expr precedent ("a uniform interface based upon expr"); his sketch excluded operator[] because it suggests a contiguous row.

Adequate. The design resolves the tension between the two comments in favor of expression reads with no pointer route, and names the fallback (remove the row expressions from both families). G12 notes that the mandated bf16_chunk override serves a test-only path.
Q4. Is the smaller parent scope sufficient? Proposed: yes; expression reads and the existing typed bulk operations; slices, iterators and generic writes deferred.
Ben's review: "the usual operations that we expect of tensor types and, in particular, the row-wise load/store operations".

Adequate. The deferrals are explicit and reasoned. G39 asks to restore the one sentence that mapped append_v_row to the sketch's store_row, so Ben sees the name difference explained; the maintainer judge also asks for a sketch-name to design-name table.
D5. Who owns native-K typing? Requested scope: the issue author; reuse the existing K view type through a new alias and change the native-K kernel parameter.
jhan's request ("introduces the new abstraction on VNNI-V and native K") and the issue title; not part of Ben's sketch.

Right attribution, one wording slip: the cell says "reuse the existing view alias", but const_native_k_view is new in section 5; the view type is what exists (G04). The record is copied into the PR description, so fix the cell before implementation.
jhan's step-4 premise (the child's packed-K change becomes a local change within the new type) and the identity of "the issue author", "the assignee" and "the user".
Two notes: the premise is answered nowhere, and it holds only in part (G37, N56 residual); the three role labels for one person are never tied together (G35). Neither blocks implementation.

judges.label: Implementing agent's view
judges.reasons: I could start building the parent from this page today. The forward declarations, the owner, the view, the row expression, and the three typed operations (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token) have declared signatures and stated semantics [design-r3.txt:232-260]. The accessor table gives every existing caller a replacement [design-r3.txt:264-277], the two kernel signatures are complete [design-r3.txt:277], the arena construction names the array placement-new form, its two entry points, and the arena filter [design-r3.txt:338-352], and the step table and behavior-check table name files and evidence [design-r3.txt:371-378, :434-445]. Every source fact I rechecked matches live main 1400fa4481, which is identical to 2880c3aa9b for every file the parent touches [facts-r3.md:40-43]. I would stop once, at step 2. Line 249 restricts detail::v_vnni_access (the friend function that returns the packed pointer) to typed tensor operations and V-specific kernels and says cache callers do not use it [design-r3.txt:249]. Line 273 makes detail::scaled_v_expr, which lives in kv_cache.hpp, take the packed view [design-r3.txt:273], and line 329 says it obtains the physical address only inside the typed implementation [design-r3.txt:329]. Today that struct reads the address itself through reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size)) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2016-2018]. The page does not say whether scaled_v_expr may call the friend accessor or must move into v_vnni.hpp. Two implementers would resolve this differently and produce different PR shapes on the PV weighted-sum path, which runs on every decode step, so the design owner should choose (G01, major). A second, smaller gap: the PV case of t_amx_numerics hand-packs a std::vector<bf16> page and passes v_page.data() to weights_times_v_128x4 [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203-227]; the typed signature rejects that pointer, and the page names no fixture route (fixture = a test's prepared input data) for this test, although the route is derivable from the fixture exception at line 317 and the owner's as_view() [design-r3.txt:317, :237-238] (G22, minor). Neither gap makes an implementer build the wrong thing, and either resolution of each merges, so the design is implementable now; the verdict is "accept with changes" only because G01 is a contradiction in the design text on that path. The 24 partly items and 2 deferred items are wording, citation, and evidence-labeling residuals; I confirmed the S18 label swap (the [Main generated save call] link points at the save_k_helper emission at ingest/src/TronCpp.hs@30c4ac82cb:2338 and the [Helper] link at the save_k emission at :2406) and the four LoopyTronSpec assertions that change (ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs@30c4ac82cb:2801, :2812, :3225, :3231), but none of these changes what gets built. The 8-lane class-completeness rule is right as the code stands: the fake kernels at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:180-190 sit outside the #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH at :192. Separately, 64 finding links and 2 page links point into claude-review-design-new-tensor-type.html [design-r3-links.tsv], the file this round's review overwrites, while the round-2 page is archived as -r2.html; repoint them (G03). The Q1-Q4 + D5 record is adequate for both readers: each row carries a proposed choice, the effect of rejection, and a status; the owner is named as jhan-positron; posting is gated on the owner's authorization; Q2 states and explains its departure from the sketch's span-like const rule; D5 attributes native-K typing to the issue author, not the reviewer [design-r3.txt:83-101]. judges.label: Maintainer's (Ben's) view
judges.reasons: The design answers all three of my comments. Comment 1 (the worker index, r4065141577) is answered by merging save_k and save_k_helper into one save_k(..., worker_ix = 0, n_workers = 1) and deleting the helper entry points [design-r3.txt:420-424]; the child's two generated call sites exist where the design says (save_k_helper at ingest/src/TronCpp.hs@30c4ac82cb:2338, save_k at :2406). Comment 2 (review 5270587330) asked for an expr-based packed tensor with row-wise load and store operations; the design gives v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view and v_vnni_row that inherit expr, plus append_v_row, load_row and copy_token [design-r3.txt:238-240, 255], and it types both kernel arguments [design-r3.txt:277]. Comment 3 (my sketch, 5765866077) is followed on every point I would insist on: an aligned owner with lvalue-only as_view [design-r3.txt:238-239], private pointer construction with mutable-to-const conversion only [design-r3.txt:248], bounds-checked at() [design-r3.txt:245], the arena constructs the real storage type and never casts the old SIMD array [design-r3.txt:344-352], no clearing is added [design-r3.txt:118, 346], k_storage is selected by std::conditional_t [design-r3.txt:399], and the page accessors and the AVX-512 fallback take typed views [design-r3.txt:404, 407]. Where the design departs from the sketch it says so and asks: the address formula lives in the view (Q1, which matches my own stated doubt), const applies at both ranks (Q2), operator[] returns a non-contiguous logical row (Q3), and the first scope is smaller (Q4) [design-r3.txt:95-98]. Nothing is attributed to me that I did not write: the ids and times in the table match the saved JSON (18:24:52; 18:53:47; 18:58:31 edited 18:59:58) [design-r3.txt:67-69; evidence/github-review.json], "drafted his GitHub sketch with his own Claude session" paraphrases my "Claude and I came up with the following straw-man" [design-r3.txt:46], and every proposal is labelled "Proposed; reviewer answer not recorded" [design-r3.txt:95-99]. One phrase is stronger than what I wrote: "the reviewer's uniform-expression requirement" [design-r3.txt:412]; my review said "I think the way I would approach this". The one gap I would not let implementation start with is my own boundary rule applied to scaled_v_expr. The design says the internal accessor is for typed operations and V-specific kernels only and that cache callers do not use it [design-r3.txt:249]. It also says scaled_v_expr obtains the physical address only inside the typed implementation [design-r3.txt:329]. But scaled_v_expr is cache code in kv_cache.hpp that dereferences a raw bf16s* today [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1990-1993, 2087-2088], and the design does not say which rule wins. My sketch allowed "SIMD and AMX implementations" to use the helper, so the design should say that scaled_v_expr is such an implementation, or it should move the body and list that move. The same silence covers the t_amx_numerics PV fixture, which passes a std::vector<bf16> pointer to weights_times_v_128x4 today [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203-227] and has no permitted typed route under the design's rules (no public pointer construction, no test use of the helper). Smaller slips: D5 calls const_native_k_view "the existing view alias" [design-r3.txt:99], but the alias is new in kv_cache_fwd.hpp [design-r3.txt:232]; the type it names is the existing one (const_view<bf16,true,false,seq<R,C>> with the row_major default stride sseq<C,1>, h/tron/tensor/views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:31-36, kv_cache.hpp:2215-2219). The accessor names are not parallel (page::v_view versus page::k_packed [design-r3.txt:271, 404]) where my sketch used v_packed and k_packed. The headers diverge from my single h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp into v_vnni.hpp and k_vnni.hpp [design-r3.txt:391]; round 2 judged that no change required (N59), and I accept it as the design's choice. The verdict is accept with changes: the interface and the decision record are what I asked for, and two short text edits settle the only questions an implementer could get wrong.

judges.label: Risk reviewer's view
judges.reasons: The design now states the numerics, lifetime and concurrency rules an implementer needs, and I checked the load-bearing ones against source. The NaN table is right: fp32 0x7F800001 truncates to bf16 0x7F80 (+infinity) in the packed append, and the generic conversion gives 0x7F81 (a NaN) only when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is absent [design-r3.txt:334; h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp@f46e48ba:92-109]. The existing padding test poisons the odd row through page::set_v with a float quiet NaN (0x7FC00000, which truncates to 0x7FC0 and stays a NaN), so the design's poison route survives the removal of v_data [design-r3.txt:436; t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:2776-2792]. Today's packed set_v already uses aligned source loads (_mm256_load_epi32 for bf16 and fp16 rows, _mm512_load_ps for float rows), so the design's 64-byte aligned-source rule preserves an existing precondition rather than adding a new crash risk [design-r3.txt:257; kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2300-2312, :2380]. The constructor sets storage_slot_count_ in its initializer list before it calls allocate_kv_group, so slot enumeration inside the construction helper sees the right slot count [design-r3.txt:348; kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1091-1103]. A placement array-new probe on a trivially destructible 64-byte-aligned 32,768-byte block returned the same address as the arena at -O0 and -O2 with g++ 11.4 (clang 19, the pinned compiler, is not available on this host), so the construction form at design-r3.txt:344 is low risk. Pair-write serialization and one-lane-per-line K stores are stated [design-r3.txt:318-319, :410]. Two gaps stop a compiling first draft. detail::scaled_v_expr lives in kv_cache.hpp, reads the pair-tile base through reinterpret_cast of a raw bf16s pointer, and receives kv_block.v[0] from page::scaled_v [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2016-2017, :2085-2086, :2260-2261]. The design forbids cache code from using detail::v_vnni_access, requires a packed view in that constructor, and names no route from the view to the tile base [design-r3.txt:249, :273, :329]. The AMX PV numerics case passes a hand-packed std::vector<bf16> to weights_times_v_128x4 [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:188-219]. The typed parameter has no pointer route, and the design names no typed route for this test [design-r3.txt:277, :377]. One CI risk needs a stronger done criterion. The kernel call sites in self_attention.hpp are inside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH [self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1571, :1654, :1680]. The required Nix lane never sets that option [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:79-102]. The fakes at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:47-190 compile in every build, so required CI catches a declaration mismatch but not a broken typed caller. The design asks for the AMX-on build [design-r3.txt:453], but the definition of done only says that build is reported separately [design-r3.txt:498]. The 24 partly and 2 deferred residuals are wording, citation and evidence-hygiene items. None makes the agent build the wrong thing. The G04 slip (D5 says reuse the existing view alias, but const_native_k_view is new in section 5 [design-r3.txt:99, :232]) is a wording fix, not a decision gap.

verdict_outro: What changed since round 2. Round 2 named four major gaps; all four are closed or reduced to wording (N01 resolved, N02 resolved, N03 resolved with G16 and G17 as the header-home residue, N04 resolved). The one major of this round is new: it appeared when the round-3 edit deleted the sentence that kept scaled_v_expr in kv_cache.hpp while tightening the access rule. Every other new finding is a wording, citation or process item, and the checkers found no regression among the 87 known items.

What the design does not have to do. It compiled nothing and ran nothing; it posted nothing and edited no issue; sw-dev-01 is codex's user rule. None of those is a finding. Ben's answers to Q1 to Q4 are not needed to start: the design says to implement the proposed choices and label them Proposed in the PR description, and all three judges accept that.
rejected_intro: These candidates were refuted by at least two of the three verifiers, or dropped by the lead after reading the votes. They are listed so a reader can see what was considered and why it did not hold; the votes page carries the full reasons.
method: This round used the same shape as round 2, with more finders. The lead first re-verified the facts the design relies on (comment-site line ranges, CMake and Nix flags, workflow steps, child names) against the pinned commits and refreshed the live state of main, issue #4525 and PR 4424; that record is evidence/claude-review-r3/lead-verified-facts-r3.md.

Numbers of this round: 234 agents, 28.2 million tokens, 2 hours 15 minutes; 17 disposition batches (51 agents), 10 finders, 1 merge agent, 52 merged candidates with 156 verifier votes, 1 critic with 4 candidates and 12 votes, 3 judges. The workflow result is evidence/claude-review-r3/workflow-result.json; the inner result (the script's return value) is workflow-result-inner.json.
method_bullets: Dispositions: 17 batches of 3 to 7 items; per batch one checker and two re-graders (source-truth, fairness); majority of three; batch files in evidence/claude-review-r3/batches/.

New findings: 10 finders (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben and jhan, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs, regression hunt on the round-2 to round-3 diff, section-9 honesty audit), plus new defects the checkers found in the fixes; one merge agent deduplicated; three verifiers (source, design-text fairness, intent) per candidate; a finding survived when at least two could not refute it; the lead read every vote before grading.
Completeness critic after verification; its candidates went through the same three verifiers.
Three judges (implementer, maintainer, risk) read the design and the review summary independently.

Limits: no code was compiled or run; no chromium on this host, so the page was checked structurally (ASCII, anchors, links) and not rendered; agents can make mistakes, so every finding carries its evidence and votes; the lead's own reading is not a substitute for Ben's.
Evidence: evidence/claude-review-r3/ holds the workflow result, findings.json, build_findings.py, gen_review.py, overrides.json, the design text and word diff, the facts file and the batch files.
